title: Explore deformation at lower values differs
description:
I have a customer case, where the deformation values on the lower end of the legend differ a lot in Explore stage. 
In the above example, the higher end values (red in color), closely match with Refine, Mechanical as well as Optistruct (the application customer uses, and wants to compare the results with). Where as the values on the lower end (Blue in color) on the same location differ a lot. These values are small in value, and the difference does not seem like a lot, but in percentage it in order of 50+%. Is this due to the size preview being bigger than the deformation?

On the bug discussion, here are the few additional points that came up.
1. At what resolution are you testing? What GPU is being used?
Ans: I am running it at the highest fidelity (100%, standard) on a 16GB VRAM. During the run, it was reaching 12-14GB of VRAM usage. The size preview is at 0.2mm. (The user likely has a smaller GPU). The higher value is within a 5% error margin, and the behavior matches well, but the user also checks the lower values on the pot side of the caliper, which is part of their practice. Therefore, it’s important for them to see that match as well for them to adopt Discovery.

2. Observation by Matthew: I'm concerned that the simulations they are comparing between Discovery, Mechanical, and Optistruct are not the same.  The deformation shape is different.  If you look at the "ribs" on top of the device, they have minimal deformation in Mechanical but medium deformation in Discovery.  I think there is some disagreement in loads/boundary conditions.
Ans: The Refine and Mechanical ones are transferred from the same Explore run. I do not think there could be any difference in the boundary conditions as such.

3. As per Rabii: I think this is a bug about pressure condition. results are fidelity dependent: with a voxel size= 0.49mm discplacement is wrong.


Do let me know if any more information is needed. We have also tried using Force (using the area where we are applying the load, and the pressure value), those results also differ significantly, and do not match well with Optistruct.

title: Surface bodies are not visible in Mechanical
description:
Dear all, I hope you are fine. I have a customer's model, in which two of the surface bodies are not visible in Mechanical. However, they do exist. They are selectable and a mesh is created for them. This issue is observed in block E, in the bodies: 
'Tele 3 (4 Mio.+)' --> 'Teleskop3_Schalen(Tele 3(4 Mio.+))'-->'Oberschale vorn 6mm(Tele 3 (4 Mio.+))' and 'Unterschale vorn 7mm(Tele 3 (4 Mio.+))'

These two surface bodies come from block G. So, I opened block G Geometry and noticed that Telescope3_Schalen is in Shared Topology (Properties tab). I set that to None and created the Shared Topology for this part using Prepare tab (I think this was an old bug which is supposed to be corrected). Then I refreshed everything, and the surfaces are visible in block E. The problem is that everything loses scoping (contacts, Remote Points, materials etc..). So, is this indeed related to Shared Topology? Is something else I can do, in order not to lose scoping of everything, or is it related to something else?

Please, find the model in this link: 00161109-Bodies not visible in model assembly

Also, in the ds.dat file the elements are written correctly for these two bodies that do not appear in block E, and if I click on Show Mesh the meshing appears for these two bodies. So, is this solely a graphics bug or does it affect the analysis too?
Thank you in advance.

Kind Regards,
Stella

title: LM_PROJECT and IDLE - Heartbeats after CLIENT_ACTIVE call do not have LM_PROJECT value set on Windows
description:
ARM test idle-003 shows this issue on Windows. 

This test does the following:
  1. Sets idle timeout in the FNP options file. 
  2. Sets: "INCLUDEALL PROJECT test_project" in the options file.
  3. Checks out licenses with the LM_PROJECT=test_project value set.
  4. Makes and idle call and let the licenses go idle. 
  5. Makes an active call to check back out the licenses.
  6. At this point is where the defect occurs... After the active call, ACL starts back up the FNP heartbeats for the license feature that went idle but it does not pass the LM_PROJECT value "test_project". Because of this the heartbeats fail to reacquire the license, and the client go into LOST mode.
  7. In LOST mode the first RECHECKOUT attempt does pass the LM_PORJECT value so it able to checkout. 
The issue as stated above is the heartbeats cannot reacquire the license correctly because it is missing the LM_PROJECT value when going to FNP.

title: UI does not show a correct band plot when modifying a radio with scripting
description:
I testing this on the EDT v26.1 certified build with EM Installer dated on 08/28/2025, UI does not show a correct band plot when modifying a radio with scripting. This defect occurs only when doing it through scripting (Scripting Only). No issue with performing manually. 

Here is the plot between scripting and non-scripting
* From scripting, if I manually disable/enable Harmonics, it will show a correct plot.


To reproduce this defect (Scripting):
  • Launch EDT, add EMIT design
  • Select Tools > Open Command Window

  • Type these command:
    oProject = oDesktop.GetActiveProject()
    oDesign = oProject.GetActiveDesign()
    oModule = oDesign.GetModule("EmitCom")
    oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("SchematicEditor")
    radio_id = oModule.CreateEmitComponent("Radio", "New Radio", "Radios")
    oEditor.ZoomToFit()
    band_id = oModule.GetChildNodeID(0, radio_id, "Band")
    rx_spetral_id = oModule.GetChildNodeID(0, band_id, 'Rx Spectral Profile')
    oModule.SetEmitNodeProperties(0, rx_spetral_id, ['Enabled=false'])
    tx_spetral_id = oModule.GetChildNodeID(0, band_id, 'Tx Spectral Profile')
    harm_id = oModule.CreateEmitNode(0, tx_spetral_id, 'Harmonics', 'Custom Tx Harmonics')
    oModule.SetEmitNodeProperties(0, harm_id, ['Harmonic Table Units=Relative'])
    harm_table = '2;-50'
    oModule.SetTableData(0, harm_id, harm_table)
    oProject.Save()
  • Open a Radio configuration. 
  • Select a Band node. You will get a result shown above.
These are steps to do manually on the EDT:
  • Launch EDT and add EMIT design
  • Add a radio in the schematic window.
  • Open a radio configuration
  • Expand a Band node and disable "Rx Spectral Profile"
  • Right click on "Tx Spectral Profile" and select "Add Custom Tx Harmonics"
  • Change "Harmonic Table Units" to Relative
  • Select Add  Row and insert these value
  • Select Band node again to see a Band plot.

title: Rotor Back Iron heat dissipation not displayed in the output tab
description:
A mismatch between Dissipation TVent Total and sum of individual table values has been identified. This discrepancy comes from a postprocessing bug. The Rotor Back Iron to Through Ventilated Fluid heat dissipation is not listed in the table. However, it is being included in the total summation.

That is why the Dissipation TVent Total is a little bit higher.

This migth be worked out by summing the powers shown in the Schematic manually. By doing so, it has been noticed that these values are missing from the table.

The screenshot below shows two of the three resistances. If the Rotor Back Iron to Through Ventilated Fluid heat dissipation values from the schematic are added to the values in the Dissipation table, it equals the Dissipation TVent Total.

title: Discovery custom beam profiles get transferred to Mechanical as new ones upon dimension change
description:
In 2025R2 Discovery, some custom beam sections are created of type Disk. These sections are then transferred to the downstream Mechanical system accordingly.

Assume a change is made to a dimension of the cross section in Discovery. The properties of the cross section are changed accordingly in Discovery (used to be a bug in 2025R1). Now, when updating the geometry in Mechanical, the cross section is imported as a new one and re-assigned as the active cross section of the line body.

This behavior theoretically works fine, but practically adds to the data that Mechanical has. What is many changes are made to the Discovery geometry for testing - we would then have an accumulation of beam profiles in Mechanical for no reason, as they wouldn't be used. I would expect that the beam profile definition gets overwritten in Mechanical - same as it happens in Discovery (no addition of new profiles upon dimension change).

title: Generic Connector: CLI Crashes on Invalid or Incomplete Option Usage Instead of Providing User-Friendly Errors
description:
🔁 Reproducible Scenarios

❌ Scenario 1: Invalid --auth:mode value

%ANS_MINERVA_CLI% --auth:mode --help

Result:

System.InvalidOperationException: Failed to convert configuration value at 'auth:mode' to type ...

---> System.ArgumentException: Requested value '--help' was not found.

❌ Scenario 2: --interactive used without a value

%ANS_MINERVA_CLI% --help --interactive

Result:

System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.

   at Ansys.Minerva.IntegrationFramework.Common.Utility.FindInteractiveMode(String[] args, ...)

❗ Expected Behavior

  • The CLI should not crash or throw raw exceptions.
  • It should detect invalid or missing values and return a clear, user-friendly error, such as: Error: Missing value for --interactive. Valid values are: None, Console, Graphical. or Error: '--help' is not a valid value for --auth:mode. Valid values are: Explicit, Impersonate, Refresh_Token, Windows, Browser.
  • Ideally, it should also suggest: Use '%ANSMINERVACLI% help ' for more information.

✅ Suggested Fixes

  • Add input validation for all CLI options.
  • Catch and handle exceptions like ArgumentException, IndexOutOfRangeException, and InvalidOperationException.
  • Provide fallback help messages when invalid input is detected.
  • Consider implementing a generic help parser that can intercept malformed input and redirect to appropriate help content.

📎 Additional Notes

  • The CLI currently handles unknown verbs gracefully (e.g., Verb '--path' is not recognized.), which is a good pattern. This behavior should be extended to invalid option values as well.

title: Published Live Value PACZ from MC MBSE fails to run in MCD
description:

Steps to repeat the issue/error

  • Using 1Day_Turbofan_Tutorial1_startingFile.mdzip
  • Before adding to the server, I reset IDs in Cameo to be able to upload project
    • Same project existed from another upload

 

Recursively checked out the Turbofan model from TWC

 

Followed the MC MBSE training tutorial to build analyses

  • Integrated calc_SpecificThrust scriptwrapper
  • Created the Requirements verification diagram with satisfy relationships
    • Created constraint blocks from the requirements satisfy relationship
    • Imported requirement constraint blocks into MC MSBE
  • Added requirements to the execution plan
  • Ran to verify requirements

 

Published the Execution plan that was created.  In publishing login gui

  • Select Live value from TWC
  • Specify TWC Server URL
  • Fill in login info
  • Select Trust invalid certificates

 

In the publishing gui:

Select all the Model.LiveInputs.Turbofan… variables

Select Model.Requirements… Variables

 

Specify a folder in the local MCRE directory to save the published PACZ file to

 

Save the MC MBSE Execution plans and results

Close MC MBSE

 

In Cameo, Collaborate > Commit changes to server

 

In ModelCenter, create a new process workflow

From the Server Browser, add the published PACZ to the workflow

Open all the elements under the component to see the properties

Run the component to update the properties

title: DPF: dpf.operators.math.matrix_inverse() output changed from build 2025-04-16 02:08 P01
description:

Use the following script to reproduce the issue:

import mech_dpf
import Ans.DataProcessing as dpf

scoping = dpf.Scoping()
scoping.Location = "Nodal"
scoping.Ids = [1, 8, 14, 20, 26]

dpf_0.Scoping = scoping

for i in range(nmodes):
    for j in range(nmodes):
        if j >= i:
            op.inputs.fieldA.Connect(disp[i])
            op.inputs.fieldB.Connect(disp[j])
            MFieldCont = op.outputs.field.GetData()
            ijData = MFieldCont.Data[0]
            FIM[i*nmodes+j] = ijData
            FIM[i+j*nmodes] = ijData

matrix_r = dpf.FieldsFactory.CreateMatrixField(1,nmodes,nmodes)

matrix_im = dpf.FieldsFactory.CreateMatrixField(1,nmodes,nmodes)

MFieldCont = dpf.FieldsContainer()
MFieldCont.Labels = ["complex"]

MFieldCont.Add(matrix_im, {"complex": 1})
matinv = dpf.operators.math.matrix_inverse()
matinv.inputs.fields_container.Connect(MFieldCont)

title: TurboGrid: hybrid mesh volume fails for larger global size factor
description:
For the GE Vernova turbine blade, hybrid meshing fails for the hub after setting the global size factor to 2:
Volume meshing failed.

The shroud hybrid mesh was successful. See attached state file and Prime files. For the pmdb see the linked defect.

Note that the overall meshing time is more than two hours.

title: TurboGrid: hybrid mesh has significant mismatch in boundary layer elements
description:
For the GE Vernova turbine blade, hybrid meshing on the shroud end shows significant mismatch between the hex mesh and the unstructured mesh where the boundary layer expansion in the hex mesh is large due to the blade concave curvature (common for turbine blades). This causes extreme stretching of the mesh elements and low mesh quality. Other than reducing the number of inflation layers in the unstructured zone, I see no other workaround. This is most likely an enhancement request, but I'm recording it here for now.

See linked bug for files.

title: PyModelCenter: Cannot create a DOETool component programmatically
description:
Unable to create and configure a DOE Tool component from pyModelCenter. See the following teams message for more information:


I'm having issues actually making an example script setting up a DOE though. Is there some trick to setting one up programmatically, or even from the GUI? If you drag/drop a DOE component straight into ModelCenter, it comes in with no variables, so I can't really set anything. It seems like you have to add some design variables through the DOE GUI before it works.

Maybe it's just an issue with the DOE Tool component plug-in. I think it should probably do what the OptTool does. I'm using an example script that creates an Optimization. Or maybe it isn't allowed. I see some other plug-ins doing the same thing, like the RSMToolkit or Excel.
Steps to Reproduce:
  • Download the attached python script
  • Change the path to the DOE component to point to the path on your local devbox
  • You can uncomment the code or just run through to see the issue. I don't know if the commented-out code actually works. I made it based off of an example in pyModelCenter, so I suspect it should be close. Either way, after running this you should see a new model with two components. One will be the DOE with nothing available. Trying to interact with it, such as setting the algorithm, will fail.

title: In FilterQuick, component value are set incorrectly for Low Pass/High Pass/Band Stop Butterworth filter (with default parameters) when checking 'Update All Capacitors'
description:
In FilterQuick, component value are set incorrectly for Low Pass/High Pass/Band Stop Butterworth filter (with default parameters) when checking 'Update All Capacitors'.

To reproduce:
1. Launch Ansys Nuhertz FilterSolution v252.
2. In Filter Quick window, select 'Lumped Synthesis' design, choose 'Butterworth' as filter type, choose Low Pass/High Pass/Band Stop. Keep the default value of the parameters. 
3. In the Circuit panel, select a component, like capacitor. In the popped up 'Modify Lumped Filter...' dialog, in 'Type Change' group, check 'Percent'. Check 'Update All Capacitors'. Modify the number from 100 to 90. Click on 'Apply'. In the Circuit, all the capacitors' value are changed to 80% instead of 90% of their default values .

title: AEDT: Invalid report values
description:
In our ParameterConversion.xslt file, we assume that the AEDT "Materials" table values will always be numbers. For this attached file, that is not the case - extraction was failing because the <number> value is not a number.

We put in a PR to work around this: Pull request 593302: Fix for handling bad AEDT report values - Repos which will comment out any bad values in a report and log a warning to the consolidated metadata log. 

The root of the problem, however, is that AEDT is putting invalid values in this report. I'm assuming that this is not specific to just this attached file, though the issue has not been seen/raised before. I made this bug to track the AEDT issue.

This is an example of one of the invalid sections. The value should be a number instead of the string we're seeing:

title: DPM-Blocking + Ideal Gas violating conservation of energy
description:
I am testing this case in which a particle at 90 deg C is placed inside an air container with all walls and initial temperature equal to 90 deg C. The container has one opening with 0 (gauge) pressure. 



The expected behavior is to observe a constant temperature throughout the simulation. However, this is what is happening:

Rocky 25.1.2 + Ideal Gas + Porous Media formulation



Rocky 25.1.2 + Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking: The fluid temperature increases indefinitely, causing the particle temperature to increase.



Rocky 25.2.0 + Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking: Same as 25.1.2 + Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking

Rocky 25.2.0 + Incompressible Ideal Gas + DPM-Blocking: Behaves as expected. 


Rocky 25.2.0 + Ideal Gas + Eulerian Multiphase:  Works



In summary:

Ideal gas + Porous media ✅

Ideal gas + DPM Blocking ❌

Ideal Gas + Eulerian Multiphase  ✅

Incompressible Ideal Gas + Porous Media ✅

Incompressible Ideal Gas + DPM Blocking ✅

The project files are attached.

title: Fluent users should have the flexibility to retain their chosen working directory throughout the session.
description:
We are in the process of organizing our V&V tests using a structured folder setup for CFD simulation types. Our goal is to provide customers with ready-to-run test cases, where they can simply execute the provided journal files without needing to modify the setup.

Please find attached a sample test case for your reference. The folder structure is organized as follows:

  • Pre-Processing: Contains all input files
  • Solve: Stores case and data files
  • Post-Processing: Stores output files
  • Reports: Stores generated reports
However, we’ve encountered an issue: Fluent does not retain the working directory specified by the user in the Fluent launcher.

Steps to Reproduce:
  • Download the attached sample test.
  • Launch Fluent.
  • In the Fluent launcher, set sample_test as the working directory.
  • Select Meshing mode and PyConsole (Beta).
  • Run Run1_Meshing_3D.py from the Pre-Processing folder.

Expected behavior: Fluent should maintain sample_test as the working directory.
Observed behavior: Fluent changes the working directory to Pre-Processing.


This behavior disrupts the intended automation flow and may confuse users. We believe users should have the flexibility to retain their chosen working directory throughout the session.

Could you please look into this issue?

title: Preserve variable separator rows when importing/exporting variable dialogue, and other variable dialogue suggestions
description:
This submission is copied and pasted from ELE-I-2481, which was determined to be a defect.

To organize variable lists, labeled separator rows in the variables dialogues are frequently used. The variable dialogue export/import process does not preserve the separator rows. As a result, when the export/import process is done, the resulting variable dialogue looks disorganized and more difficult to read.

The example shown below is simple, so does not demonstrate the real importance. For most most customer designs, separators are very helpful for usability/readability.

Original

Export

Imported into other design (missing separators)


1) Please ensure that the variable dialogue export/import looks identical to the original source, including separators.

2) The default save directory for exporting the variable dialogue is PersonalLib > 3D Components, which does not make sense to me because variable sets tend to be tied to specific projects, not 3D components. The default export/import directory should be the same directory as the selected project if the project is already saved to disk. If the project is not yet saved to disk, the user should be prompted to save the file to disk. The directory browse option should have a button option to "Last Variable Export Save Location", which should be preserved within and between AEDT sessions. This option is in case the user wants a quick way to specify an alternative location for saving variable sets.

3) The design variable export dialogue has two options

a) "Include referenced project variables", which seems to only export design variables, so should probably be labeled "Include design variables"

b) "Include all project variables", which exports design and project variables, so might be better labeled "Include both design and project variables"?


The attached project is what I used for testing. The project has both project and design variables and separators in both dialogues.

title: MCD 25R2 Golf: Creo plug-in leaks temporary directories when run
description:
The CAM Creo plug-in leaves some temporary folders laying around after it is run.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Download the attached file.
  2. Create a new workflow.
  3. Drag the Creo plug-in into analysis view.
  4. On the Initialize PACZ window, choose 'No Files Needed'.
  5. On the Add a New Component window, keep the Save Style as Expanded PACZ Folder and specify a name (or accept the default name) and press OK.
  6. Browse to & select the tool_densityset.prt file and click Open.
  7. Select All variables and click OK to close the Select Variables window.
  8. Click the Apply button and close the Creo Plug-In window.
  9. Run the workflow.
  10. Save the workflow.
  11. Close ModelCenter.
  12. In File Explorer, go to the PACZ folder that was just created.
  13. Observe that it has a temporary directory (e.g. 2bc9ac4d-0631-4f95-b89f-bf3882b34374) in it.
  14. Go into the temporary directory and observe that it is empty.

Environment Details:

  • OS version: Windows 11
  • Application version: ModelCenter Desktop v2025 R2 Golf
  • Java: Java 17

Expected vs. Actual Behavior:

  • Expected Behavior: The temporary directories should be cleaned up automatically after the Creo plug-in is run.
  • Actual Behavior: The temporary directories remain in the PACZ folder even after the Creo plug-in is run and closed.

title: PyAnsys Sound / SAS - the class SoundComposer has no project name
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
This class: SoundComposer — PyAnsys Sound is the main class for working with a Sound Composer project with PyAnsys Sound.
However, a project has name in SAS, but this name does not exist in PyAnsys Sound, which causes several problems:
  • when a project is loaded from a file, its name cannot be found
  • when a project is created in PyAnsys Sound, then saved into a .scn file, then open in SAS, there is no name displayed in the GUI
    • side effect: the name cannot be set in SAS' GUI
    • workaround: if the Sound Composer GUI is maximized, then reduced, the text field to set the project's name is now working correctly
Data:
Sound Composer project file: SoundComposer-WhatIfScenario-Motor-Gear-HVAC-Noise (SMA modifications).scn

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
Bug 1: 
Load a Sound Composer project in PyAnsys Sound
Print the project -> no name is displayed
Display its name -> not possible (no command to do this)
This name should be the same as the one displayed in SAS: 


from ansys.sound.core.sound_composer import SoundComposer

sound_composer_project = SoundComposer(project_path="SoundComposer-WhatIfScenario-Motor-Gear-HVAC-Noise (SMA modifications).scn")
print(sound_composer_project)



Bug 2:
Try to display or set the name of the project
-> not possible, no member nor method of SoundComposer allows to set or access the name of the project.

Bug 3:
Save the Sound Composer project above
sound_composer_project.save(project_path="My_Saved_SoundComposer_Project.scn")

Reopen it in SAS
-> no title is displayed in the GUI
-> the title cannot be edited in the GUI
(NB: is the window is maximized, then it works again)


Expected behavior:
When loading a .scn file in PyAnsys Sound, the name of a Sound Composer project is read,  and accessible.
When working with a Sound Composer project in SAS, the project name can be set, modified, displayed.
When saving a Sound Composer project with PyAnsys Sound, the name is saved in the scn file, so that opening this file in SAS or PyAnsys Sound allows to get this name.
(in other words: in class "SoundComposer" add a @property called "name", a @setter, and use it in load and save methods. Optionally it would be a good idea to add an argument "name" in the constructor)

title: Imprint splits curves and does not track objects (result.GetCreated[IDesignCurve]() not supported)
description:
Imprinting curves on a face splits them at any intersections. This impacts lists of the original curves. Then, result.GetCreated[IDesignCurve]() does not work with imprint either. Not splitting the curves would help (although this might impact other workflows), but it'd be best to track the created curves if possible to fix this issue.

# Python Script, API Version = V251

ClearAll()

# Create Box
result = BlockBody.Create(Point.Create(MM(-10), MM(-10), MM(0)), Point.Create(MM(10), MM(10), MM(20)), ExtrudeType.ForceAdd, Info1)
# EndBlock

# Toggle 3D Sketch
result = Sketch3D.Set3DSketchMode(True)
# EndBlock

curves = List[IDesignCurve]()

# Sketch Line
start = Selection.Create(GetRootPart().Bodies[0].Edges[2].GetChildren[ICurvePoint]()[0])
end = Selection.Create(GetRootPart().Bodies[0].Edges[4].GetChildren[ICurvePoint]()[1])
result = SketchLine.Create(start, end)
curves.Add(result.CreatedCurves[0])
# EndBlock

# Sketch Line
start = Selection.Create(GetRootPart().Bodies[0].Edges[3].GetChildren[ICurvePoint]()[1])
end = Selection.Create(GetRootPart().Bodies[0].Edges[6].GetChildren[ICurvePoint]()[0])
result = SketchLine.Create(start, end)
curves.Add(result.CreatedCurves[0])
# EndBlock

# Imprint Curves
options = FixImprintOptions()
options.Tolerance = MM(0.5)
result = FixImprint.FindAndFix(options, Info2)
new_curves = result.GetCreated[IDesignCurve]() # Related command does not track objects, unable to process request.
# EndBlock

title: Ansys Motion coupled case with excessive overlap when using Automatic Communication Step Size
description:
A customer reported he was detecting particles crossing the geometries in an Ansys Motion - Ansys Rocky coupled case. After investigating customer setup, I initially tought the issue arised from the excessive refinement of the triangles in certain geometries or due to relatively low YMs (1e+07 Pa for Particles and 1e+09 Pa for Walls).

However, even after restoring triangle tesselation to its original size and increasing YM (I even tried with 1e+09 Pa for particles and 1e+11 Pa for walls), I still was seeing excessive overlap messages and particles crossing walls. 

One point is that the behaviour always started at 3.55s of simulation, no matter the parameters:
 

I don't know if this is a coincidence or not, but it coincides with the moment of higher rotational accelaration of the geometry:


When I changed the Communication Step Size control in the MBD FMU module to Solver Step Size, then the case is running without excessive overlaps (even with 1e+07 Pa as Particles YM) and already passed the "critical point". But it slows down simulation pace.


Steps to reproduce:
  • Open attached case (\\CDCW16RALLY02\TFSProd\Attachments\Rocky\1314390) and run
  • Check that at 3.55s of simulation, the particles will accelerate and start leaking from the geometry (Increasing YM 100x did not help)
  • Changing Communication Step Size control to Solver Step Size in the MBD FMU module and run
  • Check that the particles stop "exploding" and simulation is slower.

title: 3D Layout - Layer Stackup Wizard Etching Calculation Convention Inconsistent with 3D Layout Model Editor
description:
Layer Stackup Wizard etching profile is inconsistent to 3D Layout Modeler. For instance, see attached project.  If you open layer stackup wizard and compute the desired trace width for 85ohm differential impedance, you would get trace width of .07mm.  However, this number is misleading, as it is the underside value (i.e. the shorter "etched" width for the trace).  The expected value is .105mm.  It is also inconsistent with the 3D Layout modeler window,  



This only becomes obvious when exporting the design to Q3D: 



I think general convention would be that a user would be expecting the line dimensions to be the maximum, and that etching would result in one side being less wide.  This is how the 3D Layout modeler handles it, as running the SYZ sweep on .105mm trace widths give 85ohm TDR:





Hopefully this is clear - the modeler needs a value of .105mm to see 85ohms in the TDR, but the Layer Stackup Wizard needs a value of .07mm.  Both are correct, but the side of the trace it is referring to is different between the two.  Please let me know if you need more clarification.

title: Surface Mount 3D Component Connector S-parameters Differ Between 3DL and HFSS at Low Frequencies
description:
The below two projects compare 3DL and HFSS for a surface mount connector on PCB.  The HFSS model was created by exporting the 3DL model and then adding the 3D component for the connector.

SurfaceMountConnectorOnPCB_WithResistLayers_3DL_2025R2.aedtz


SurfaceMountConnectorOnPCB_WithResistLayers_MCAD_2025R2.aedt


There is a top soldermask/resist layer in both that intersect with the connector, but both 3DL and HFSS seem to handle the overlap.  The S-parameters above a few GHz match well, but below 1GHz, the 3DL model appears to have an open circuit.  Green is S21.  Red is S11.  HFSS is solid lines and 3DL is dashed lines.  The red circled part shows the 3DL green dashed S21 sharply coming down at low frequencies. 

At 100MHz, the 3DL S21 = -2.28dB, while HFSS S21 = -0.011dB.



A discrete sweep from 1MHz to 1GHz with logarithmic x-axis (using the same trace colors and solid/dash representations) shows that the low frequency behavior deviates dramatically.  HFSS has the solid green S21 trace near 0dB across the frequency span, while the 3DL S21 decreases to less than -35dB by 1MHz.


Plotting ComplexMagJSurf for both at 1MHz does not show a substantial difference in surface current distribution despite transmission being 35dB worse in the 3DL (left) case.  Port 1 (the coax port) is turned on for both, with port 2 (the stripline port) being turned off.

However, looking closer, the ground pin currents in 3DL appear to be discontinuous:

Zoomed side view of the same red arrow annotated previous image:

In contrast, the currents appear continuous in HFSS:

Could the connector ground pin bottom surface in 3DL be disconnected from the vias top surface, thereby creating an open circuit?  

The respective via objects seem like they should span all the way to the top of the "Top" layer.

title: Issue with failed designs with OCO when MC is restarted (and optimization resumed)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BAE Systems) noticed that OCO, once halted, attempts to resume from the very start of a trade study, while they are expecting it to resume from the last completed run.

Original Email to @Mike Belcher with more technical details to ask if this is the intended behavior for OCO:
Technical Context
  • ModelCenter Configuration: MC 25R1
  • Workflow: Control a CATIA parametric model, which is then used in an in-house CFD code
  • Optimizer: OCO
    • Max Number of Design Evaluation: 5000
    • Seed = 1
    • Use MOP = True
    • A lot of failed designs in the first iteration (with 501 Design Evaluation).
Observed Behavior
  • The customer runs MC on a box, which communicates with other boxes.
  • This control box crashed and was restarted, leading to a relaunch of MC.
  • Upon restart, MC recovered the data, the optimization GUI appeared with the 'Resume' option and the Design Explorer Table.
  • The last recorded entry in the design table was column #34.
Resume Issue
  • When the customer pressed 'Resume', the counter restarted from 1/501 instead of 34/501.
  • CATIA attempted to reopen but almost immediately failed.
  • A successful run typically takes ~5 minutes, while a failed one takes ~1 minute (because CATIA crashes).
  • The customer reported that 19 out of 34 runs failed in the first iteration, estimating a ~20-minute latency between hitting the 'Resume' button and resuming from column #34 with a newer design point. I asked him to provide this quick time estimate, as I felt it could be useful for understanding the behavior and diagnosing the issue.
Reproducibility
  • The same behavior occurs when pressing 'Halt' followed by 'Resume'.
Additional Notes
  • The customer cannot share the model and described the issue verbally while testing live, without screen sharing.

Internal Test on Toy Workflow on MC25R2
Please see the image below, along with the attached model and video.
Objective:
To verify whether the initial setup completes quickly up to the point where the trade study was previously halted—suggesting that cached values are being reused.
Setup:
Very simple function, y=log(x), to be minimized, with x defined in the range [−5,10] and a starting value of 5.
Since y cannot be evaluated when x<0, the solver fails in those cases.
Results:
It appears that when OCO is halted and resumed, it restarts the initial run. Moreover, the first set of runs takes just as long to complete (10 seconds) as the subsequent ones, indicating that caching may not be working as expected.

This behavior can easily be observed using the BEE plugin.

  1. Set the license server to one you can monitor.
  2. Install BEE.
  3. Use the BEE plugin to create a PACZ for the balloon ride sample that comes with BEE.
  4. Open Tools -> Preferences.
  5. On the Trade Studies tab, set it to run locally with 3 copies.
  6. Create an optimization with the DAKOTA Coliny DIRECT algorithm.
  7. Run the optimization.
  8. Observe that only one PowerShell console comes up to run BEE.
  9. Observe in the license manager that only one moxie_sysml license is checked out.

    Expected vs. Actual Behavior:

    • Expected Behavior: The DAKOTA Coliny DIRECT optimization algorithm should run multiple instances in parallel, utilizing multiple licenses.
    • Actual Behavior: The optimization algorithm runs only a single instance, checking out only one license.

title: MC 25R2 Golf: Geometries don't always completely render the first time
description:
Description:ModelCenter doesn't always fully render geometries the first time. This issue affects geometries in both the Geometry View and embedded geometries in the Analysis View. Switching back and forth between Geometry View and Analysis View will cause them to fully render.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Download and extract the attached zip file for the MCI Basic training.
  2. From the MCRE Files folder, copy the mci_training_basic folder and paste it in the MCRE analysis folder.
  3. Start ModelCenter Desktop (MCD) and load the answer for Tutorial 6.
  4. Observe that the embedded geometry on the right may not have fully rendered.
  5. If the embedded geometry didn't fully render, switch to Geometry View and then back to Analysis View. Observe that the geometry is fully rendered now.
  6. If the embedded geometry fully rendered, switch to Geometry View and observe that the geometry may not have fully rendered. Switch back to Analysis View and then back to Geometry View. Observe that the geometry is fully rendered.

Environment Details:

  • OS Version: Windows 11
  • Application Version: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 Golf
  • Java: Java 11.0.20

Expected vs. Actual Behavior:

  • Expected Behavior: Geometries should fully render the first time without needing to switch views.
  • Actual Behavior: Geometries do not fully render the first time and require switching between Geometry View and Analysis View to fully render.

title: Replay of journal does not change Physics Settings for Explore Fluid simulations
description:
Develop after   https://tfs.ansys.com:8443/tfs/ANSYS_Development/CASL/_git/Disco/pullrequest/602855 was merged

Blocking creation of a regression test for Class 3 bug 1284242.

Changes in Settings > Physics to fluid flow settings for the Refine and Explore stages are recorded in a journal.  However, replay of the journal only implements for the Refine stage.

Fig. 1 shows the settings after changes to:
  • Modeling method, Meshing method, Max. iterations and Target engineering convergence in Refine
  • Modeling method, Target stopping criteria in Explore

If the Disco defaults are re-set and then the journal recorded for the changes is replayed in a new Disco session, Fig. 2 shows that only the parameters for the Refine stage are implemented. Changes to the Reference Pressure cause a parse error though.

title: Meshing Fails After Sharing Topology Between a Surface and a Solid Body
description:
I was able to reproduce the issue on my end , even with simplified models. Specifically, in a structured setup like following, when using the "Share Topology" tool from the Prepare tab, the common surface body is merged into the solid body. As a result, it is not imported into Mechanical. (System C of attached project)


 
Following this, the mesh generation process fails and becomes stuck at 5%.
 
Given that this behavior appears to be problematic ,I am raising this bug report for further investigation. 

In the meantime, a workaround is available:

In ANSYS Discovery, locate the two or more surface bodies within the same component.

Set the Transfer Sharing Option to "Share Topology."


 
Ensure that the "Merge" option is disabled under the Share Topology settings.

With this configuration, the geometry will be imported into Mechanical with shared topology, but the surface body will remain unmerged. This allows the mesh to be generated without issues.
 

 
I hope this explanation is clear. Please let me know if you need any further clarification.

title: Default Keyframe coloring error when using project context export
description:
Genentech is using the project context feature as they have several similar simulations and want to use the tool to facilitate similar post-processing. When they try to export the context, they run into the following error:



After some discussion, we believe that the cause of the error is due to the fact that the project was originally created in a previous version in which the property Coordinate: Y (which is used to color the 3D view used in the animation panel) was named differently (y-coordinate if I remember correctly). 

Steps to reproduce:
  1. Open attached case and run 1 output
  2. Try to export the context
However, it seems that it is possible to workaround that by refreshing the keyframes in the animation panel.
Workaround:
  1. Refresh all the animation keyframes in all 3D views
  2. The export should go through now
In my tests that was enough, but for the user, she had to also clean the AppData/Roaming/Rocky/Settings folder

It would be great if the Keyframes could be automatically updated with the new property, but we should at least have a warning to the user to update the keyframes when we run into this error.

P.S. Another user, MacDon, which is evaluating their renewal of Rocky has reported the same issue.

title: [GPU Remapper] Missing NodeZoneExchangeDefinition from Fluent
description:
To reproduce the issue,
  1. Launch fluent.exe with 3ddp_debug -t2 -gpu=-1 -gpu_remap=-1
  2. Create any Node monitor of surface that contains partition in Fluent.
  3. Cromwell crashes inside ReconstructNodalValues(...) located at ..\NodeFieldReconstruction.cxx
Reason:
  • Node zone exchange is incorrect in case of Gpu Remapping and it led to wrong nodeset exchange definition. (look at CreateAndSetExchangeDefinitionForNodeSets(..) at nodesetutilities.cxx for implementation).
  • ReconstructNodalValues(..) use those wrong nodeset exchange definitions and crashes. 
  • Possible fix would be to account for remapping in AddMeshNodeZoneExchangeDefinitions(..)(located at ..\fluent\src\gpuapp\..\gpuapp_mesh_interface.cpp)

title: Installing 25R2 over 25R1 corrupts installation; SAM Connector fails; registry state not recovered by uninstall/reinstall
description:
Installing 25R2 on top of 25R1 leads to a broken environment. Indicators point to missing/incorrect registry keys after the upgrade.

Notes:
    - Uninstalling 25R1 and then installing 25R2 does not fully repair the system; issues persist.
    - In at least one case, the SAM Connector installer failed within the installer (appeared not to unzip a sub-package), preventing SAM from working.
    - Applying registry exports from a “good” machine to a broken machine increased errors, suggesting fragile or environment-specific keys. (Note: this was done as a potential workaround for Kyunghun (ACE) and is not advised for end-users) 

- Impact:
   
    - Users can easily enter a non-functional state during common upgrade behavior.
    - SAM Connector and potentially other connectors fail to install or run.
    - Field users already impacted; more reports likely as 25R2 adoption increases.
    - Recovery unclear; may require full cleanup of products and registry, which is risky.
     
- Affected Versions/Env:
   
    - From: 25R1 existing installation
    - To: 25R2 installation on top of 25R1; also observed issues after uninstalling 25R1 and installing 25R2
    - Users: Internal test machines (Ajay), field user (Kyung Hoon, South Korea)
    - OS: Windows (registry-related)
    - Components: ModelCenter core (MC/MCRE/MBSE mentioned), SAM Connector; other connectors appear OK in clean 25R2 (per Don’s usage)
     
- Repro Steps (current understanding):
   
    1. Start with a machine that has 25R1 installed.
    2. Install 25R2 over the top of 25R1.
    3. Observe missing functionality and/or connector failures (MC desktop fails to start due to licensing error, SAM connector fails to start due to assembly mismatch).
    4. Optional: Uninstall 25R1 and reinstall 25R2; issues may persist due to registry state. (large portions of registry under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Phoenix Integration` appear to be missing in at least one case) 
    5. Attempt to install/use SAM Connector; installer errors and/or SAM not present/working.
       
- Expected Result:
   
    - Installing 25R2 over 25R1 should either:
        - Perform a safe in-place upgrade that preserves/updates all required registry keys and components, or
        - Block with a clear message and guide the user through a supported upgrade path.
    - Uninstall/reinstall should restore a clean, working 25R2 environment, including SAM.
     
- Actual Result:
   
    - Post-upgrade environment is broken. SAM Connector fails to install or run; installer may fail to unpack a sub-package.
    - Uninstalling 25R1 and reinstalling 25R2 does not reliably repair the environment due to lingering/broken registry keys.

title: 2025 R2 AEDT Icepak DE: Result mismatch when in AEDT when using bool and edb files for ecad
description:
This context comes from a previous customer workflow where they compared results between Classic Icepak and AEDT. The comparison involved importing a .tzr file from Classic Icepak into AEDT, which included ECAD data imported as .bool files in AEDT. They observed a temperature difference of approximately 5–6°C for a specific die, with AEDT reporting the lower value.

The customer is currently testing a new workflow. They begin by importing the ECAD files into HFSS, then export them as an EDB (.def), which is subsequently imported into an existing Classic Icepak project. This project is then exported as a .tzr file and opened in AEDT.

To account for the loss of the solder mask layer—originally present in the HFSS file—the customer ensures that solid blocks are created in AEDT to represent the solder mask when importing the .tzr file. This step involves the use of the .bool file

Additionally, the customer is evaluating a parallel workflow. In this approach, after importing the .tzr file into AEDT, they replace the PCB geometry (originally represented by .bool files) with the original HFSS models. Since the HFSS files include the solder mask layers, the customer ensures that any existing solder mask blocks previously created in AEDT are disabled to avoid duplication.

Across all workflows, the material properties, grid cut resolution, and mesh settings remain consistent

In this case the AEDT result with tzr (.bool) is not matching with the one with EDB. Surprisingly the AEDT results with the edb (.def) matches with the classic results and is enquiring if the new workflow is alright and want to know the root cause of the issue.

I was able to reproduce the varying results in AEDT ie. With bool and edb file for a single board. The results vary by ~ 2 oC here.

Does this have to do anything with the difference in ECAD. I ‘m unable to match the mesh number even if it uses the same mesh settings in both cases. This more of the case to investigate the work flow as customer is transitioning to AEDT and the consistency of the results are critical for them.

Kindly investigate.

Note: For reference I am attaching a aedtz file with the bool and edb import,and the original edb file.

title: Auto-save can break ChangeProperty() calls
description:
Restore the attached archive in desktop, then run the attached script.  It should work fine.  Then, in general options make sure autosave is on and set the autosave interval to just 1 edit.  Close the project, reopen from the archive, and run the attached script again.  This time it shows an error that the Renorm Imped property doesn't exist.

It seems like auto-save hitting on the first ChangeProperty() call in the script causes it to malfunction--it should be adding Renorm Imped as a property, but doesn't.

This was first discovered in a branch by a failure in the emit regression test SBR_DL_Mismatch_Renorm.  On that branch the number of edits triggered by the test script before the "Do Mismatch Renorm" ChangeProperty() was upped from 9 to 10, causing the test to begin failing with the error above when run in ARM as it uses 10 edits between autosaves.  So I don't think setting the autosave interval to 1 is required to trigger the error, but the script has to be such that the autosave happens during a particular call.

Test Impact:
  • EDT_EMIT:Coupling/SBR_DL_Mismatch_Renorm

title: Through Hole Connector 3D Component Results Different in HFSS vs 3DL; Potential Artificial Short Circuit in 3DL?
description:
A through hole connector 3D component in HFSS yields expected propagation characteristics in HFSS, and unexpected apparent short circuit behavior in 3DL.  In both models, the through hole connector signal and ground pins overlap pad and via geometry.

The connector launch to PCB in HFSS is shown below using a clip plane view.  The signal path is from the connector signal pin to a stripline  on the orange, metal layer 2.  The field is terminated in a wave port with 0.03mm thick metal backing.



S21= -0.1dB at 1GHz, which is a reasonable response

A Remote Point with Deformable behavior should not be used on surfaces that are modeled with symmetry boundary conditions. The internally generated weight factors only account for the modeled geometry. Therefore, remote points with deformable behavior should only be used on the "full" geometry.

title: Big discrepancy of iron loss calculation between Motor-CAD and Maxwell
description:
Hello Team,

       We have a customer to compare the core loss calculation between Maxwell and Motor-CAD.
       Motor-CAD model is using "Bertotti – Maxwell" model to calculate the iron loss, and then export it into Maxwell. 

        The coefficients of kh,kc,kdc, etc. are correct in Maxwell model, that have corrected numbers generated by corresponding coefficients from the Bertotti – Maxwell model.
        Both Motor-CAD and Maxwell models have same 90 steps per cycle and the meshing is similar between them, and I also adjust meshing (results are same).
     I use “Maxwell” and “Bx, By” as you mentioned in Motor-CAD.
     Maxwell model reaches the steady state in the core loss results.
     
     However, I find stator core loss of Motor-CAD model is about 11% higher than Maxwell’s results, and rotor core loss is 40% higher than Maxwell model.

      For 40% difference, it does not make sense for the calculation tolerance. 
      Could you check if it is a defect? Thanks.






Best regards
Howard

A customer is simulating a custom geometry in Motor-CAD v25R1. It works fine in Motor-CAD and gives the results as expected as well.

But when customer exports the model in Maxwell 3D using python script, these issues are coming:

  1. Even though the model is symmetric, the symmetry factor is not being considered in the script, and it doesn't split the model to create the partial geometry. The geometry stays to full model only.
  2. The machine is with 3 tangential magnet segments, and orientation for those magnets are not being assigned correctly.
  3. Some of the magnets are being assigned with Vaccuum material.

I have attached the script and exported 3D Maxwell Model for your reference.

Let me know if any further information is required.

Regards,
Anil.

title: getDSMesherSweptInfo takes a lot of time -> MultiZone takes about an hour to generate ~10K mesh
description:
I had this case from Joao Read in ACE today where he was struggling to mesh it but I found that it was just actually taking a very long time to mesh with MZ and if he had waited (he did not)  he would have seen a really perfect mesh. 



it takes 54mins on my laptop to generate this 10k element mesh



but if I merge top/bottom faces I get this in 2.5mins: 




So a couple of questions (1) can we make this faster? If we were to submap surface mesh the top face and use pull/thinsweep to mesh the volume would it be faster than using mapped blocks? title: [AEDT Circuit] Simultaneous tuning for two LNA setups does not update successfully the respective traces of a report.
description:
Electronics Customer Bug

Description
Issue:
See the attached archived project (“Bug_Project” – please keep it CONFIDENTIAL after the customer’s request).

In the Circuit design (“Circuit1” design) of the attached project, although the “Tune” box is checked/enabled for both the LNA setups of it, when you change the value of each tuning variable (moving the slider up and down) in the “Tune” window, only the traces that correspond to the first LNA setup are updated successfully in the report, as you can see in the attached screen recording (“Issue.mp4” file).

If only one of the two “Tune” boxes is checked (e.g. only the “Tune” box that corresponds to the “Ch9” LNA setup), then the traces of the report, that correspond to this setup, are updated successfully, each time you change the value of the respective tuning variables.

The issue above is contradictory with the highlighted text of the screenshot below (from the Ansys Circuit Help pdf for version 2025R1 of AEDT):



So, based on the above, this issue seems to be a defect/bug.

As a comment, this issue has been brought up to our attention by a customer and I managed to reproduce it in the current version of AEDT (2025R1), as well as in previous versions of AEDT (e.g. 2024R2.1, 2024R1.1).

Could you please take a look at the issue described above and let me know if it is indeed a defect/bug or if it is the expected behavior of the software? If it is a defect, is there any workaround for the time being, until it is fixed?

Thank you in advance for your time and your input!

--


Reproducible: (always, sometimes, never)
Always in every version of AEDT.


Steps to reproduce:
1. Open the attached archived project (“Bug_Project” – please keep it CONFIDENTIAL after the customer’s request) and run/analyze the two analysis (LNA) setups (“Ch5” and “Ch9”).

2. Double click on the “S Parameter Chart1” report, in order to bring it in the “Active View” window.

3. Right click on the “Optimetrics” tab in the “Project Manager” window-> select the “Tuning…” option.

4. In the pop-up window (“Tune” window), check the “Tune” box for both the analysis (LNA) setups (“Ch5” and “Ch9”), uncheck the “Browse Available Variations” checkboxes and change the value of the tuning variables using the respective slider each time.


After following the steps above, you can see that only the traces, that correspond to the “Ch5” LNA setup, are being updated in real-time in the “S Parameter Chart1” report ; the traces that correspond to the “Ch9” LNA setup are not being updated in real time.

title: Motor-CAD slowdown when multi-parallel running by OptiSlang
description:
Hello Devs,

Attached, you will find an OptiSlang model that calls several Motor-CAD instances. The purpose is to compare the calculation times required. The analysis is system-dependent, but we can observe the same trends in the following operations:

AVERAGED ->  OptiSLang Sequential (excl Design 3)  OptiSLang 2 Parallel OptiSLang 4 Parallel OptiSLang 6 Parallel OptiSLang 8 Parallel


Time-Start MotorCAD 5.708 10.05425 21.215 40.2615 54.42125

The time required to simply open multiple Motor-CAD instances (with or without the black box) is increasing. For example, it takes ~6 seconds to open Motor-CAD when solving multiple designs sequentially, but it takes about 54 seconds to open a single instance when asked to open 8 in parallel.

We expect some delay when solving Emag and building the Lab (no multithreading), as this is a result of CPU utilization, so it is not a concern.

However, another operation that is questionable is the solution for the Duty Cycle and Efficiency Map. Regarding Duty Cycles, it is possible that customers may request a duty cycle with multiple points, which could dramatically increase the calculation time. Is there a way to make these operations scalable?

Time-Lab Duty Cycle 6.996 8.707 12.24275 20.328 27.85825
Time-Lab EffMap 11.533 13.884 21.05125 32.86775 54.49625

@Dougie Hawkins @Daniel Bachinski

title: Possible problems with particle size check for SPH simulations
description:
Warnings for SPH element size when it is not small enough to resolve the particle might be misleading for Custom Polyhedron and Assembly shapes in certain circumstances. The minimum sizes were over-estimated in the below tests, which might lead to simulations running without any error/warning but producing incorrect results. In all tests the SPH element size was set to 0.05 m to trigger the warnings/errors. The Rocky simulation archive and the STL file for the I-beam are attached to this report. Two trials were made with the attached case:

Trial 1:
Here, an I-beam shape particle was tested, which was created as a Custom Polyhedron and imported as STL. The triangle size for this STL was set to 0.01 m. This shape has the smallest thickness at its centre as in the below screenshot:

However, on Rocky Status Panel, it captures the minimum particle size as 0.1 m.

Trial 2:
In this test, sphere, sphero-cylinder, and their assemblies (screenshot below) are checked. Sphere diameter is set to 0.01 m, and sphero-cylinder sieve size is set to 0.005 m with aspect ratio of 2. Rocky captures the minimum sizes of the sphere and spherocylinder correctly in the Status Panel. However, for the assembly, it prints out that the minimum particle size is 0.00999 m, while the smallest dimension in the assembly should come from the spherocylinder with sieve size of 0.005 m.

title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 BETA: FMU Plug-In does not pick up on defined bounds for variable
description:
Not sure if this is a bug or a feature request, but basically: 

Using the attached .fmu project, there is a variable named "e" that is defined in the internal .xml file, like so:

    <ScalarVariable name="e" valueReference="6" causality="parameter" variability="tunable" initial="exact" description="Coefficient of restitution">
      <Real start="0.7" min="0.5" max="1"/>
    </ScalarVariable>
    <ScalarVariable name="v_min" valueReference="7" variability="constant" description="Velocity below which the ball stops bouncing">
      <Real start="0.1" declaredType="Velocity"/>
    </ScalarVariable>

In the context of the FMU plug-in from ModelCenter wrapping it, we do pick up on the "Real start" value being "0.7", but we miss or don't pick up on the min and max bounds defined right next to it. From a user's perspective, this would probably be a welcome feature, instead of having to manually set the bounds that are already defined anyway.

title: Page connector allowing connection between non-conservative and a conservative pin
description:
The attached project (Ansys SSCB 0319_25R1) is originally from Bug 1223354. In the design 4 P1_SSCB_PWM14 phase closer_GaN_wrong=, output of PWM1 is connected to Page Port S1. And then the conservative pin (Gate) of the Spice model IGC033S101_L1 is also connected to S1.

Usually UI warns such illegal connection (as far as I checked with 25.1). So I'm not sure how the AE established this connection. 

In the netlist, there is no connection is actually established between PWM1.VAL and the Gate of IGC033S101_L1. But from the schematics point of view it appears both are connected. 

If I try this in a new project (see PageConnNonConservative_FromScratch251.aedt) in 25.1 UI, the netlist generator error outs as follows:

    [error] Netlist error due to unconnected pin "GATE" for component instance "IGC033S101_L1_1", design "TwinBuilder1"

This is the correct behavior. So not sure why it doesn't show it on the original project.

title: MCD Geometry Node doesn't support "Appearance'
description:
Geometry objects have an appearance that can control their color and alpha.
The Node does not support this: see a SOR, QuadFacet and Node all set to use_parent_color:

Presumably this is because the color can be specified, but it doesn't have to be.  
Node is the only geometry type where the color can be specified, but it doesn't support alpha or defaulting to the GeomInfo Appearance.
Would be great if Nodes didn't specify used the Appearance, or if there was some blending of the node color and the Appearance setting.
This may be a feature request, but nodes not coloring with the appearance when all the other geometry types feels like a bug.

Picture came from linked model: GeomNodeIgnoresApperance.pxcz

$T2 = 10 kelvin

title: MC MBSE Ansys SAM 25R2 RC: Requirement attribute expression doesn't show Type or expression value in Analysis Editor
description:
Screenshot is attached. 

  • What happened?: When loading the "TIE copy CMB SAM25R2 sample model - Electric Powertrain Battery Sizing and Verification1" example into MC MBSE, the attribute "testExpression" under the "Minimum Operating Time" requirement shows "Type" as "Unknown" and the Requirements Details pane shows a blank value. The expression is only identified when attempting to link it to an Analysis variable, where a tooltip indicates that linking expressions to analyses is not supported.
  • What should have happened?: The "Type" should show as "Real" and the expression value should be visible in the Requirements Details pane or as a tooltip.
  • Where does it occur?: Analysis Editor in MC MBSE
  • How often does it occur?: Always


According to User Story 1227068: Allow connecting requirement attributes to analyses as both inputs and outputs , the expectation is that we show the value of the expression as a value or tooltip.

Repro Steps:

  1. Load the "TIE copy CMB SAM25R2 sample model - Electric Powertrain Battery Sizing and Verification1" example.
  2. Search for "testExpression" in the project search bar and note that the Definition is set to "Real" and the Value is set to "1 + 1" (no quotes).
  3. Open the workflow in ModelCenter using the web File menu.
  4. In the MC MBSE window, choose to Edit the "Mater Out (Copy)" analysis from the Analyses pane.
  5. Expand the "0-1 Minimum Operating Time" requirement to the "testExpression" item and also expand the "Requirements Details" pane at the bottom.
  6. Attempt to drag the "testExpression" attribute to another variable like "inMass" and observe the tooltip indicating that linking expressions to analyses is not supported.

Expected vs. Actual Behavior:

  • Expected Behavior: The "Type" should show as "Real" and the expression value should be visible in the Requirements Details pane or as a tooltip.
  • Actual Behavior: The "Type" shows as "Unknown" and the Requirements Details pane shows a blank value. The expression is only identified as being one when attempting to link it to an Analysis variable.

CLOSING SUMMARY:

Cause (if regression set a SPEOS_REGRESSION tag):

This issue seems to be due to the Speos loading process. There is no issue when using NX without Speos...
Also, the issue appears when opening/loading the part for the second time (not the first time).

Load of SNX feature is done when entering in Speos application (not with NX callback)
  • First load:
    • Post Load callback are called (not used by SNX)
    • Display callback are called by NX (but no callback are registered for SNX at this step)
    • Entering in SNX application:
      • SNX callback are created (valid for all the session)
      • SNX feature are loaded and created
  • Second load
    • Post Load callback are called (not used by SNX)
    • Display callback are called by NX : In each display callback SNX load features to display them and add dependencies in MODEL reference set and add dependencies to the display : PROBLEM

Solution:

Don't load SNX features in entering application callback but implement Post Load and manage missing dependencies that are not loaded

title: File definition separator works incorrectly with only a space defined flags
description:
If a comma is not specified in the separator attribute, the variable and value are not picked up in the input file.  I attached 2 examples, one is for creating a variable and the number from the input file.
The second example is for reading a string from the same input file.  If the input file does not include comma separators between the string values in the line, the string values to associate with the variable are not picked up.  Commas were required to find the arguments.  This will be an issue since many standard input files will have spaces as separators between values in a single line.

description:

title: Gap detection standalone and scripting issues (part 2)

- Open and Run the gaps_script_v2.dscript script

- Use the Detect tool with the Find small gaps option and create named selections from selections
- With the Measure tool, check a few of the other named selections to verify that some face pairs do have a gap

title: API for get solder info error setting calibration factor
description:
When invoking the API to get solder info, it can cause a NullPointerException.

Steps
  1. Copy the attached solder.csv file to the user settings directory at: C:\Users\<user name>\AppData\Roaming\Sherlock. I did not edit this file. It was created by Sherlock. I don't know how it got in this state, but I assume this can happen from normal use.
  2. Launch Sherlock with the command line option: -grpcPort=9090
  3. Invoke the SherlockCommonService.getSolderInfo API. This can be done with a tool like Kreya or from PySherlock, including running the test_common.py unit tests.

Result
Sherlock doesn't send a response. A NullPointerException occurs. This happens because the CC Calibration Factor is null and the generated GRPC code doesn't allow setting the string field value to null.
This is an unhandled exception.

The following is output to the console: 
10:24:11.569 java.lang.NullPointerException
10:24:11.572 	at sherlock.grpc.SherlockCommonServiceProto$SolderInfo$Builder.setCcCalibrationFactor(SherlockCommonServiceProto.java:10131)
10:24:11.578 	at sherlock.grpc.Service.SherlockCommonService.getSolderInfo(SherlockCommonService.java:176)
10:24:11.581 	at sherlock.grpc.SherlockCommonServiceGrpc$MethodHandlers.invoke(SherlockCommonServiceGrpc.java:690)

When this is invoked by PySherlock (when running the test_common.py unit tests), it causes the following error: 
E               Failed: <_InactiveRpcError of RPC that terminated with:
E                       status = StatusCode.UNKNOWN
E                       details = "Application error processing RPC"
E                       debug_error_string = "UNKNOWN:Error received from peer  {grpc_message:"Application error processing RPC", grpc_status:2, created_time:"2025-06-05T15:24:11.5519384+00:00"}"
E
Expected
No exception occurs. If this is an error case, then that error should be returned in a response.
If it is ok for the CC Calibration Factor to be null, then this field should not be set and the solder info should be included in the response.

Additional notes
This also happens using the latest code for 26.1.

title: Model not working correctly, results conflict each other
description:
In the attached project file (keep confidential), when the customer simulated only the cutout, they obtained the expected low insertion loss in the passband (5–7 GHz). However, when they simulated the full board, they observed a high insertion loss in the passband (5–7 GHz), whereas they were expecting similar low insertion loss as with the cutout. I removed the encrypted 3D component and added two 0.01 Ω resistors between the top transmission line and the two bottom transmission lines, and I got −3 dB loss at DC for each transmission line, which is expected since this works similar to a Wilkinson power divider. This experiment confirms that there is no open or short in the nets connecting the top transmission line to the bottom transmission lines. It looks there is an issue when the encrypted 3D component is added to the full board. I simulated the full board model with and without mesh fusion in both 2025 R1 and 2025 R2, and obtained the same results. I also exported the board as a layout component to HFSS and observed similar behavior, both with and without mesh fusion.

title: Icepak and Q3D both behaving improperly with temperature-dependency in Joule feedback
description:
Both Carlos and I have tried to run this model quite a few times. If you run a constant electrical conductivity setting, both the Icepak only Joule heating setup and the Q3D setup get similar answers.



I do not like the 14 C difference, but at least they're in range over the 70 C ambient.

Here's the bad part: I use a temperature-dependent input for the electrical conductivity and both behave incorrectly in this model but completely different.

In Icepak, the temperature DROPS significantly. This CANNOT occure as the conductivity is decreasing with temperature over 22 C. As such, a model that's already 400+ C over ambient and almost 500 C above the reference temperature should show a significant increase in power and inherently temperature in the looped run.



That's a 200 C drop!!

With the looped version in Q3D, there are no changes at all even though temperature-dependency and enable feedback are both selected. 



The user thinks that Icepak is more accurate than other tools (RHSC-ET, Lumerical HEAT, etc., but I'm not seeing it with these results.

Please let me know if there's anything that can be done. I tried the basic tutorial model and the behavior seems correct in Icepak so this has no real explanation behind it.

title: C_WATERCONTENT is not always visible in PEM electrolysis
description:
@Chao Han @Genong Li 

Hello Chao and Genong,

I have come across an issue where I needed to make the protonic conductivity a function of the water content.  For that I wrote a very simple DEFINE_PROPERTY-type UDF with 3 UDMs, so that the resulting value of the protonic conductivity as well as the values of C_WATERCONTENT and C_T can be visualized.

The interesting thing is that it worked on a Bosch case seemlessly while QuestOne's case has issue at seeing the C_WATERCONTENT (c, t) macro. It is exactly the same UDF, the main options of the models are the same e.g. the osmotic drag and the water content options are chosen and enabled in the Electrolysis panel. After the client failed to make it work, I got their case on my machine using exactly the same .c file and can reproduce issue reliably.

Please find attached the .c file as well as the relevant couple of the case and data files. One case file is called UDF_working (can be opened on 2nodes) and the other one is bigger (it can be opened on 4 nodes) I tried to open ithe nonworking case on 35 nodes with exactly the same output.

In the non-working case, the C_WATERCONTENT returns zero value, despite the fact that the Water Content variable under Potential in the contours panel.

This is very odd since this type of UDF does not need any parallelization considerations. The options are the same and I just wonder whether the order of their activation/deactivation might have something to do with this bug.

Kind regards,
Aleksey.

description:

Screenshot attached. Basically, and this is more noticeable if you have many Execution Plans and many open Plans and Results, but from the Workspace Explorer, if you double-click on a given Execution Plan to open it for example, but then in the open tabs, click on a different one - in the Workspace Explorer, the "selected entry" does not update to the one you clicked, the currently open tab. title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 BETA: Trying to use "Show Component's GUI" on inserted PACZ from Minerva throws error message

An error occured while attempting to determine the state of the currently active component connections.
Details: An asynchronous operation completed with an error. Type: Phoenix.OutOfProcessComponentHosting.PaczHostInternalErrorException Message: com.phoenix_int.javaplugins.PlugInNotFoundException: A plug-in with ID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 implementing Phoenix::IHarnessBuilderUI was not found.
This one is wonky because it probably is not related to Minerva at all, but in the IT-11 deliverable, trying to insert a PACZ locally the same way simply "does nothing" (will write up as a different bug). This aspect worked in the IT-10 deliverable, I should note.

title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 BETA: Cached Minerva credentials are not used / set automatically with the "Import from Minerva" plug-in
description: If you access Minerva by way of the other new features with the IT-11 deliverable, like from the File -> Open menu, then those Minerva authentication credentials are cached for the next time you do so. However, if you then go to the "Import from Minerva" plug-in, the dialog that comes up has the default "localhost" information for accessing Minerva. I feel like if the credentials are cached, that dialog should at least pre-populate with the server address and username, if not just bypass it altogether and show the relevant Minerva location, automatically authenticating.

description:
Was not sure if this was a user story or a bug, but basically:

If you do a "Save As" action in ModelCenter Desktop, and work with the local file system, the default name is the name of the already saved workflow you're using - which makes sense, from a modern Windows UI perspective. However, if you choose in the Save As dialog (which has the name populated) to instead save in Minerva, when you get to the Ansys Minerva save dialog, there is nothing in the "File Name" field. It feels "more correct" for the name of the workflow you're using to be pre-populated, so that if users are using the same-name file names between their local system and the Minerva setup, then having to enter in the name again just introduces a chance for a user to have a typo and then not have the file names match.

title: Command recorded in script for creation of line is incomplete for some models
description:
It seems that when a line is created that passes through a body and extends beyond a face, the command in a script (index) is missing some information necessary for successful replay.

When the line is contained within a body, the following commands are recorded

# Sketch Line
start = Point2D.Create(MM(5), MM(-8))
end = Point2D.Create(MM(5), MM(8))
result = SketchLine.Create(start, end)

baseSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0].Curves[0])
targetSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0].GetChildren[IDatumLine]()[0])

result = Constraint.CreatePerpendicular(baseSel, targetSel)

However, if the line extends outside the body, the command is as shown below.  The information in bold above is missing and there is an error of "invalid selection for perpendicular constraint" on the last line shown.

# Sketch Line
start = Point2D.Create(MM(6), MM(-15))
end = Point2D.Create(MM(6.00000000000001), MM(19))
result = SketchLine.Create(start, end)

baseSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0].Curves[0])
targetSel = SelectionPoint.Create(GetRootPart().DatumPlanes[0])

result = Constraint.CreatePerpendicular(baseSel, targetSel)
If the GetChildren part is added, the command is successful.

The failure also occurs where bodies overlap as is the case with a cutter body.

I have attached a project containing a simple fluid simulation and two index scripts, one of which creates a line contained within the body (Box_Line2.py) and one in which the line extends outside the body (Box_Line4_Outside.py).

title: MBSE 25.1: Embedded and Decorator modes each check out mc_level1
description:
Creating a bug for this so we don't lose track of it.

Starting Embedded Mode from Cameo/Rhapsody checks out an mc_level1 license and keeps it checked out until the vendor tool is closed. Decorator mode also checks out an mc_level1 license and keeps it until the vendor tool is closed, so if a user opens both, we check out 1 more mc_level1 than desired.

The proper fix for this is to create a shared licensing context in the vendor tool plug-in ode, but this is not possible with the current Java licensing implementation (the code the  Java wrapper is wrapping does not have any of the license context methods).

There are a couple possible other fixes that could make this better:
  1. Make decorator mode not check out a license. Need to check that a user can't run a simulation without a license
  2. Track in the Java code whether we've opened Decorator or Embedded mode and not check out a license when opening the other one (pass empty string as the command-line arg for the license name when starting mbse.exe).

title: ModelCenter 25R1: OCO algorithm with multiple objectives reports error about not converging (though convergence is not expected - should be pareto front instead)
description:
From Margherita Coda (ACE): 

Background: I'm running an multi-opti. problem in MC (ozyczka and kundu benchmark) and selected OCO as the algo to run it

But that error popped up. I'm expecting a pareto front and not a single best design as result of this opti task. This is why I'm surprised by this error but I'm missing something here.

[see attached workflow file] 

I'm expecting a Pareto front made of 5 regions. It should resemble the one on this link (from pymoo website).

In one of my tests, I got the error above AND this Pareto front, which I like!

 


It is also quite similar to the one I'm getting in oSL (see image below).

 

 

I just need more design points to improve it but the algorithm always stops with the same error after 201 runs (elapsed time: 48/51 sec), even though it seems it is going in the right direction. 


Investigation results from JED: 


The algorithm appears to be done exploring the design space after 200 runs. Looking at the pareto front in the Opt Tool, it looks very similar to the result in optiSLang:


 

The error dialog about not converging on a best design seems to happen any time you have a result with a pareto front instead of a single best design. The message is technically correct, but is not an error - not finding a single best is expected given the optimization problem. 

 

The OptTool code checks 'algorithm->IsConverged()'  (https://tfs.ansys.com:8443/tfs/ANSYS_ModelCenter/Plug-Ins/_git/OptTool?path=/solutions/applications/PHXSolver/Algorithms/optiSLangAlgorithms/oSLAlgorithmsOOP/OSLAlgorithm.cpp&version=GBmain&line=568&lineEnd=568&lineStartColumn=13&lineEndColumn=43&lineStyle=plain&_a=contents) and throws if IsConverged is false.

 

The error dialog only show up if the OptTool is added to the model and "throwErrorOptRunFail" is true.

 

Overall, the algorithm seems to be working as expected and giving good results, but there are a couple minor things that look like bugs:

  1. We should not report an error about not converging when the result of an optimization is a pareto front. This might be a change in the oSL algorithm or in our integration. This appears to be limited to the oSL algorithms. Running Darwin Algorithm on the same problem does not error and produces a pareto front.
  2. The error dialog from the OptTool still has the red bird icon.

This bug report is to fix 1. above.

title: [Regression] Student Version (26.1) Dynamic link tests fail on cdcw11ebuqasv01 due to HFSS license exhaustion (Jul 14, 2025)
description:
Three Circuit-HFSS dynamic link based ARM regression tests failed on Jul 14, 2025 when run using the Ansys Electronics Desktop Student Edition only on cdcw11ebuqasv01.
The failures are caused by HFSS simulations not launching due to the error:

Maximum licensed number of demo users already reached.
Simulation was terminated by license error.

The tests passed on July 11.

To reproduce: Launch and solve the attached projects in SV 14th July build (log files are attached as well).

To summarize:

  • HFSS components (e.g., HFSSDesign1, TeeModel) fail to simulate

  • Nexxim dynamic link fails: There is no simulation data available from the dynamically linked component

  • Circuit simulation aborts with rejected fieldsolver:X devices

  • But the HFSS design solves fine by itself (if not solved from the Circuit design)

  • The issue is only reproducible on the official SV machine (Windows 11) which is dedicated solely for SV runs:

  • The issue is not seen with 25.2, but only with 26.1 on cdcw11ebuqasv01 - even after a clean install and machine reboot.


Affected ARM tests:
  1. [EDT_STUDENT] Circuit/UI/dynamic_link/push_excitation/f_to_freq/F_to_Freq_Push_Excitation_HFSS
  2. [EDT_STUDENT] Circuit/UI/dynamic_link/push_excitation/f_to_freq/F_to_Freq_Push_Excitation_HFSS_Thevenin
  3. [EDT_STUDENT] Circuit/examples/RF_Microwave/Filters/WaveguideFilterDynLink
