description:
I tested on the EDT v26.1 certified build dated on 08/05/2025, Unusual API behavior when calling the same object ID multiple times.

To reproduce:
  • Launch EDT
  • Open "Open Command Windows" from Tools menu


  • Type these commands:
    oDesktop.RestoreWindow()
    oProject = oDesktop.GetActiveProject()
    oProject.InsertDesign("EMIT", "EMIT Design1", "", "")
    oDesign = oProject.SetActiveDesign("EMIT Design1")
    oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("SchematicEditor")
    oEmitCom = oDesign.GetModule("EmitCom")
    emitter_id = oEmitCom.CreateEmitComponent("", "New Emitter", "Emitters")
    emitter2_id = oEmitCom.CreateEmitComponent("Radio", "New Emitter", "Emitters")

    antenna_id = oEmitCom.CreateEmitComponent("Antenna", "Antenna", "Antennas")

    We included in this bug 2 types of fail
    First one is there is a real significant number of point that changed between the 2 versions
    Second one are tests with a number of point that low if you look at the total number of point but that is no low enough to ignore, for those we want to check if the point changed is valid or invalid as it not not possible to know the answer as is.

    For each folder/scenario a summary is provided below showing the number of point that changed and the property distance/intensity/both and the average percentage of the changes.

    - test Bug1139751_FBC_lidar_reset_param - folder Bug1139751_lidar_fbc_reset: Number of significative points failing 1045/1045 due to distance, difference between expected and actual 2.4% on average

title: Variation solve interruption dialog not invoked for projects with embedded scripts
description:
Embedded scripts have been integrated with variations such that when applying a variation the script is ran.

It has been noticed that the variation solve interruption dialog is not invoked for projects with embedded scripts

This erroneous behaviour is likely due to an issue with the dialog appearing when a DV was set and the script ran. A workaround was implemented in the `InterruptionHandler` class to not raise the dialog if an embedded script is present. This has resolved the issue of the dialog appearing at the wrong time but does mean this interruption functionality does not work at all if an embedded script is included.

We should look to update this such that the interruption handler is 'disabled' at the period the variation is being set and the script run. Changes when the set is occurring are expected.

The erroneous guard can be found at the start of `InterruptionHandler.IsUserChoiceNeededToContinue()` method.


Steps to reproduce
  1. Open heatsink sample project
  2. Parameterize heat
  3. Add a few DVs
  4. Open the script editor from the file menu and embed any script (option in the toolbar)
  5. Run a local update all variations
  6. Edit any variation whilst the solve is on-going [BUG: Notice the interruption dialog does not appear)

title: uninitialized variables in PartRegionMesh::get_NumNodesEZ( int* piNumNodes )
description:
While migrating model assembly c# code to dotnet, I came accross this issue where the code tries to add to the out piNumNodes but doesn't init it.

Call stack:


which calls:


which calls:




The issue is not seen in .net framework or cpp because values are initialized explicitely to zero before call.
In dotnet, values aren't initialized in the interop layer *by design* and we can't do anything about it.
In this case, I think it is a coding, at the top of the function *piNumNodes should be set to zero.


Serverity of the bug is minor in .net framework or cpp but is serious for dotnet usage.

EDIT:

here's the COM layer in dotnet core (notice the SkipLocalsInitAttribute): 

[global::System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCodeAttribute("Microsoft.Interop.ComInterfaceGenerator", "")]
[global::System.Runtime.CompilerServices.SkipLocalsInitAttribute]
int global::Ansys.Common.DotNet.Interop.AnsStdObjects.IBaseMesh.get_NumNodesEZ()
{
    var(__this, __vtable_native) = ((global::System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshalling.IUnmanagedVirtualMethodTableProvider)this).GetVirtualMethodTableInfoForKey(typeof(global::Ansys.Common.DotNet.Interop.AnsStdObjects.IBaseMesh));
    int __retVal;
    int __invokeRetVal;
    {
        __invokeRetVal = ((delegate* unmanaged[MemberFunction]<void*, int*, int> )__vtable_native[8])(__this, &__retVal);
    }

    // NotifyForSuccessfulInvoke - Keep alive any managed objects that need to stay alive across the call.
    global::System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal.ThrowExceptionForHR(__invokeRetVal);
    global::System.GC.KeepAlive(this);
    return __retVal;
}

this is equivalent to the cpp code 
int numNodes; // uninitialized 
pIBaseMesh->get_NumNodesEZ(&numNodes);

title: Regression: OSError [WinError 6] on Script Termination Using CPython261.bat and Service() Default Port
description:
Windows 11/22H4
Unified Package Name: 2025-09-01 00:44 P00
CEI Build:   fe876fe8a1
------------------------------------

CPython261.bat triggers an Ignored Exception error when running a script that starts and stops an ADR service, causing regression test failures.

---

Description

When using CPython 3.12.11 (via CPython261.bat), a script that instantiates an ADR Service object and calls `start()` and `stop()` completes with an ignored exception during process termination. The service itself starts and stops successfully, but the error occurs at script exit.

This issue does not occur with:
- Other Python versions (e.g., 3.10, 3.12.10, 3.13.4).
- Interactive execution (running CPython261.bat and executing the script line by line).
- Scripts where the `port` parameter is explicitly set in the Service() constructor.

---

Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure CPython 3.12.11 is used via `CPython261.bat`.
2. Create and run a Python script with the following structure: 
   import os
   from ansys.dynamicreporting.core import Service

   nexus = Service(ansys_installation=installation, db_directory=database_dir)  # port left undefined
   nexus.start()
   print("Server started.")

   try:
       nexus.stop()
       print("Server stopped.")
   except Exception as err:
       raise err

3. Execute the script using: 
   > CPython261.bat script.py

---

Observed Behavior

- Service starts and stops successfully.
- Upon script termination, the following traceback appears:
   ```
   Exception ignored in: <function Popen.__del__ at 0x0000022B279EE520>
   Traceback (most recent call last):
     File "D:\Ansysdev\Installs\v261\CEI\apex261\machines\win64\Python-3.12.11\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1130, in __del__
       self._internal_poll(_deadstate=_maxsize)
     File "D:\Ansysdev\Installs\v261\CEI\apex261\machines\win64\Python-3.12.11\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1575, in _internal_poll
       if _WaitForSingleObject(self._handle, 0) == _WAIT_OBJECT_0:
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   OSError: [WinError 6] The handle is invalid
   ```

Expected Behavior

- No exception should be raised when the script exits.

Impact

- This error causes the testing tool to return a "test failed" status, resulting in three regression test failures that rely on the CEI CPython interpreter.

Workaround

- Explicitly set `port=8000` when creating the `Service` object: 
   nexus = Service(ansys_installation=installation, db_directory=database_dir, port=8000)

title: Some monitors are not evaluated when a simulation is run from a script in Run mode
description:
Affects regression

Some regression tests have started to fail because monitors are not evaluated after a solve with LiveGX.  The problem seems to be specific to the running of a script in Run mode.  If Debug mode is selected there is no issue.  Also if the solve is triggered manually the monitor is evaluated.

The issue can be seen with the attached index script, which is a shortened version of a regression test that goes as far as the validation failure.
  • if the script is run in Run mode, the monitor HeatFlow 1 isn't re-evaluated after the second solve in Refine (Fig. 1)
  • if the script is run Debug mode, the monitor HeatFlow 1 is re-evaluated after the second solve in Refine (Fig. 2)
Fig. 1:  Monitors after script run in Run mode - Heat Flow 1 not re-evaluated
 


Fig. 2:  Monitors after script run in Debug mode - Heat Flow 1 is re-evaluated

title: In AVxcelerate Labs, using the "Sensor Labs" button to edit the sensor may lose changed done and saved in the "Sensor Preparation" view.
description:
DESCRIPTION:
Data:

Notes:

Steps to reproduce:
  1. Launch AVxcelerate Labs.
  2. Delete all the sensor Layout in AVX Labs
  3. Create a new sensor layout and add a sensor to it and then save the sensor layout.
  4. Click on the "Sensor Labs" button at the top of the AVxcelerate Labs window and load the same sensor layout as in the "Sensor Preparation" view.
  5. Click on the "Sensor Preparation" button.
  6. Move any sensor and click on the "Save sensor layout" button.
  7. Click on the "Edit sensor layout" button (pencil icon button at the right of the "Save sensor layout" button): the location of the sensor in the embedded "Sensor Labs" editor matches the location saved in the "Sensor Preparation" view.
  8. Change the "Manufacturer" value of the sensor layout, press the 'tab' key on you keyboard and wait for the save  icon animation to finish.
  9. Click on the "Sensor Preparation" button at the top of the window: the sensor layout is reloaded in the "Sensor Preparation" view but the sensor are still in their latest saved location.
  10. Close the AVxcelerate Labs window.
  11. Repeat steps 1 to 5.
  12. Click on the "Sensor Labs" button at the top of the AVxcelerate Labs window: the location of the sensor in the embedded "Sensor Labs" does not match the location saved in the "Sensor Preparation" view at step 5.
  13. Change the "Manufacturer" value of the sensor layout, press the 'tab' key on you keyboard and wait for the save  icon animation to finish.
  14. Click on the "Sensor Preparation" button at the top of the window: the sensor layout is reloaded in the "Sensor Preparation" view and the sensor that was moved at step 5 reverts to its initial location from step 2.

Expected behavior:

At step 8, the "Sensor Labs" embedded editor should have been updated with the latest sensor location and orientation values as it is the case when using the "Edit sensor layout" button.

Reproducible: always

title: MCRE 25.2 - QuickWrap: Temporary run directories not completely cleaned up
description:
When running the attached component from a standalone QuickWrap, the .phx_srun* directory won't be cleaned up after running or closing QuickWrap. This case leaks all of the files involved in the run. If adding the QuickWrap component through MCRE to a ModelCenter workflow, the run directory won't be completely cleaned up. The run files are cleaned up, but the run directory is left around. This requires the "Run Sharing / Handle parallel runs by:" field to be set to "Run each execution request in a temporary folder". The other settings don't create temp files.



One thing to note is that this was on the transient VMs, so the directory the temp files are saved to are in OneDrive. If this doesn't reproduce normally, it might be worth checking with a space in the path. I also haven't tested this on linux.

Steps to Reproduce:
  • Standalone
    • Download and unzip the attached component
    • Open standalone QuickWrap
    • Open the caliper.scriptWrapper file
    • Run using the "Test Run..." button
    • Close QuickWrap. Notice the temp directories and files all still exist.
  • MCD
    • Download/unzip the attached component and add it to the MCRE analyses path
    • Add the component to MCD
    • Run
    • Notice that the directories will hang around, with the last run having the temp files. After closing MCD, the empty directories still exist.

title: Ansys Installer 25R2 RC: ModelCenter Remote Execute gets installed inside of ModelCenter Desktop folder, even when installed by itself
description:
I found with the Ansys all in one installer, if you install ModelCenter Remote Execute, it will be installed "under", or as a child folder of the ModelCenter Desktop folder. This happens even if you just install ModelCenter Remote Execute by itself. 

What I expected, was that since ModelCenter Remote Execute is a separate application, that it would be "one level higher", in the same v252 parent directory that the other applications like ModelCenter Desktop and optiSLang get installed to. 

Reproduction Steps:

1) Using the Ansys all in one installer on a fresh machine or VM, choose to install only the ModelCenter Remote Execute from the list of applications in the "Connect" group. 
2) Open the Windows Explorer, and browse to the installation location of "C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v252".
3) Note that there is a "ModelCenter" folder, if you expand that, inside are the "Java Selection UI" and the "ModelCenter Remote Execution" directories. 

I'm not sure where the Java folder specifically is meant to go, probably one parent level up as well, but the ModelCenter Remote Execute folder should have a directory for itself in the v252 parent level directory.

title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R2 RC Foxtrot: SolidWorks Configuration tool lists unsupported SOLIDWORKS versions on Windows 11
description:
The SolidWorks plugin currently displays a long list of SOLIDWORKS releases from 2016 through 2024, including versions that are not supported on Windows 11, in the list of "Configure SolidWorks" options available to choose from. This matters because ModelCenter will not support Windows 10, due to Windows 10 EOL, starting with 26R1. Official guidance states that only 2022 SP2 and newer versions can run on Windows 11. The inclusion of unsupported options could confuse users and may lead to failed installations or support escalations.

 

https://www.solidworks.com/support/system-requirements

https://community.goengineer.com/forums/topic/701-solidworks-support-for-windows-11

 

Steps to Reproduce:

 

  1. Open the "Configure SolidWorks" option from the SolidWorks plug-in via ModelCenter Desktop on a Windows 11 machine.
  2. Note the "Select SolidWorks version" window that opens up.
  3. Observe that the list includes versions from 2016 up to 2024.

 

 

Expected Behavior:

The configuration window should list only the currently supported Windows 11 versions—the current SOLIDWORKS release and the two preceding releases (for example, 2025, 2024, 2023).

 

Actual Behavior:

The configuration window lists all versions from 2016 through 2024, many of which are unsupported on Windows 11 and may not even have installer packages available to customers.

 

Additional Context:

 

  • Official System Requirements: Windows 11 support begins with SOLIDWORKS 2022 SP2 and continues in later releases.
  • Community recommendation: limit version list to current + two prior to align with support lifecycles and avoid user error.

 

Recommendation:

Trim the configuration tool’s version list to only include the current SOLIDWORKS release and the two preceding releases (e.g., 2025, 2024, 2023), and retire all versions earlier than that from the dropdown.

2) Right click on Setup1 > Export > HFSS Model...
3) Open the .aedt HFSS project
4) Save the HFSS project

Upon trying to save the HFSS project, the below warning message pops up stating "This project was created with a previous version and will be saved in Electronics Desktop 2025 R2."


However, the message is wrong since the project was created in 2025R2 and opened in 2025R2.  Opening the .aedt as a text file, we see the version was written as 2021R2, which is a version 4 years old.


Perhaps the old version string "Versions(2021, 2)" is written to the exported .aedt file to allow compatibility for opening with older HFSS versions?   In theory, that would allow exported 3DL models from 2025 to be opened in HFSS versions going back as far as 2021R2?

But the warning message, as worded, is technically incorrect, and the pop-up is one more click that should not be required when working within the same version.

In contrast, a layout component created in 3DL 2025R2, then imported and saved in an HFSS 2025R2 design, does not give any version warning when done with the same version.

title: Poor sampling of material property vs frequency curve
description:
I have a customer material dataset for permeability vs frequency. In the Edit Dataset window, the curve looks perfectly fine:



However, if I go into the material library, View / Edit a material to which this dataset is assigned as permeability, and use the option "View Property vs Frequency", the resulting Frequency-Dependent Property Viewer is very poorly sampled at the lower frequencies, leading to a "linear" looking region of the plot:



Note that I have changed the x-axis to a log scale in both cases. To the best of my knowledge, this just a visualization issue due to poor sampling, as I can use a marker to visually snap to the calculated data points, which are very far from each other at the lower frequencies on the log scale. But the sampled values seem to be correct, and I can also verify any arbitrary value in an HFSS simulation with a discrete sweep using the Fields Calculator to extract permeability at any frequency.

It doesn't look like there is a way for the user to control the frequency sampling of this plot manually. Could this kind of control be added to the interface, or otherwise have the automatic sampling algorithm updated to account for cases like this? Either way, I would consider it a minor bug without any other options available.

The uploaded project (25 R2) is simplified to one object with the permeability dataset assigned. It is a customer dataset, so please do not share.

Thanks,
David

  3. Expand that and select "Remove"

User reported that "We are Getting Different Frequencies when using Different Windows Machines for a Pre-Stress Cyclic Symmetry Modal Analysis with Force Sticking Contacts". The difference was very large: 653 Hz (PowerWulf) vs 430 Hz (MyComputer).

One machine is local machine "MyComputer". The other machine is remote cluster "PowerWulf". Attached solver output files were the "solve.out" from these two machines. 

These two machines used different MPI. MyComputer used Intel-MPI while PowerWulf used MS-MPI. I tried both MPIs to run user's model in my computer. Both predicted the same results: 430 Hz. 

Different MPP decomposition method is used on these two machines. MyComputer used MESH while PowerWulf used CYCHI. Then I tried different MPP decomposition method: MESH vs CYCHI using a MAPDL command in my machine. CYCHI gave the same results as PowerWulf and MESH gave the same results as MyComputer. See attached slides.

User and I had a discussion on the results. We all think that the natural frequency predicted by CYCHI decomposition is more realistic.

Mechanical seems to have an automatic algorithm to pick the decomposition method based upon the model size and computer memory size. Now for a model with Cyclic Symmetry and Rotational Velocity BC, should we force it using CYCHI decomposition method if distributed solve is used?

Finally, if we run the same model without using Distributed Solve in my computer, it gave the same results as the one with Distributed Solve -> MESH. This is confusing, since I guess it should give the same results as CYCHI decomposition. Please check. 

User's original model with results is here (11 GB)
User's model without results is 3600RPM_Test_Powerwulf_pts-no-results.wbpz (6 GB)
My modified file with CYCHI decomposition is here (3 GB)
My modified file with without Distributed Solve is here (1.5 GB)

title: Copied Components lose local coordinate systems assigned and cannot be read into new model
description:
This has to do with Icepak components that are needed to assemble a package in full. Currently, a user must read in a PCB for the detailed traces, create a die block as a placeholder, create a CTM V1 or CTM V2 for the regular dies and create a 3DIC for said assemblies. Each is created based on the original origin definition and/or based on a surface coordinate system if creating on a die surface (source form CSV). These can be grouped, but the groups cannot be saved as a component nor can they be copied at once (all components in the group copy and then paste at the same time with regular objects). I've also tried creating local coordinate systems based on the global and assigning them to all objects rather than moving the objects into place.

In both the move instance and the local coordinate system instance, copying and pasting the components loses the move and/or the coordinate system in the paste feature and all parts go back to global 0,0,0. The part "disassembles" and the user needs a schematic to rebuild.

Please look at the attached model. AssembledPackage design is the original Icepak model with the coordinate systems assigned to the components. TestPass is the exact components copied/pasted into another design. In that design, all local coordinate systems are not recreated/reassigned and you can see the poor assembly.

title: CPA Solver fail without reporting any errors （Big Package, 88K bumps, 18 PLOC）.
description:
CPA failed to complete the solving process in a customer side, and they are seeking our assistance in debugging. This CPA project is relatively large in scale without pinGroup, with a significant number of PLOCs. Despite two weeks of debugging efforts, we have been unable to identify the root cause of the failure to solve, as the CPA Solver itself did not provide any error messages.

1.Vallidation check is OK， with any issue.

2. Run with PLOCs. There are some warnings regarding PLOCs. The reason why PLOCs have extra bumps compared to the Package is that the Package only includes a portion of the power supplies.

 * Warning: Die pin n201533 has no PLOC connections but is present in a pin group.

 * Warning: Die pin n208243 has no PLOC connections but is present in a pin group.
  Number of cores = 32

  * Detecting nets routed between components for extraction ... 
(solver Stop)

3. Run without PLOCs, When using an existing pin group (generated by PLOC) for solving, after the CPA completes the RLCG calculations, it remains stuck and fails to finish within three days, with no Spice Netlist generated in the directory. We have confirmed that the issue is not related to memory or hard drive problems.




Currently,the customer's project at  a critical R&D milestone, and they are urging us to identify the root cause as soon as possible to help move the project forward. We hope the R&D team can assist in pinpointing the problem.

title: TAU Mesh Ignores Model Resolution Mesh Setting
description:
Similar to just submitted defect 1326699 where the TAU mesh ignores surface approximation mesh operations (normal deviation and maximum surface deviation), this submission is to report that the TAU mesher also ignores Model Resolution mesh operations.  Please see 1326699 for detailed descriptions of the model.

An almost identical model setup is used as in 1326699.


The difference is that the explored variable is the Model Resolution mesh operation with different values instead of a surface approximation mesh operation.   Box2/Circle2, Box3/Circle3, Box4/Circle4, and Box5/Circle5 have Model Resolution mesh operations applied to them of 0.01mm, 0.02mm, 0.05mm, and 0.1mm respectively.

As expected, the Classic mesher has mostly sequentially decreasing mesh size as the Model Resolution size gets bigger.  There is a defective mesh in the corner of Box2 however, that should not change the conclusion that the Classic mesher is utilizing the prescribed model resolution settings on a per object basis.  Note the tetrahedra counts going from 434 for Box1 to 75 for Box5.


In contrast, the TAU mesher in design 2_TAUModelResolution appears to ignore Model Resolution mesh operations.


Design 3_TAUNoMeshOperations is the same as 2_TAUModelResolution except that the mesh operations have been deleted.  Indeed, the mesh is identical between the two, verifying that the TAU mesher ignores Model Resolution mesh operations.

Model Resolution mesh operations, similar to Surface Approximation mesh operations, can be used to great effect with substantially reducing models to only electrically significant geometry with the Classic mesher.  These methods reduce solve time and RAM usage.

The TAU mesher currently allows these mesh operations to be applied, but ignores them, and also does not notify the user that they are being ignored.

title: Structural Optimization - Correction on doc for 'Move Limit'
description:
The issue was reported by a Channel Partner on behalf of a customer.

According to the doc:

"Total Move Limit: This property enables you to define how far each node can move in total. It must be defined in length units, for example three times the element size. By default, this property is set to Program Controlled. Select the Manual option to change the value."

According to this, the Move Limit is enforced to the displacement of each node. However, after some discussion with development it seems that the Move Limit is compared against the average displacement of all nodes. The two statements are not the same, and the documentation should be updated to avoid any confusion.

Note: Please review whether this is also needed for "Move Limit Per Iteration".

Thanks!

title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1: VBScript Component "GetDirectory" returns different results depending on how you load the workflow
description:
This one was reported by a customer to Subodh, for reference.

To begin, the legacy Script component for MCD had built-in functions to access things related to the current MCD process's object, via the COM API calls. These were handy, but unfortunately were not available in the current CAM version of the VBScript. However, the customer reported to Subodh that using the following code:

Option Explicit

Sub Run
    Dim objFSO, objFolder
    Set objFSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    Set objFolder = objFSO.GetFolder(".")
    MCdirectory = objFolder.Path
End Sub

Sometimes he would get the expected result (a string for the directory path his workflow resided in), but sometimes it would instead be the path for the MCD installation directory. 

Through testing, Subdoh narrowed it down to *how* you open the workflow. If you launch it by double-clicking on the saved workflow pxcz file, then when you run that component, it would return the directory that the workflow was saved in. However, if instead you launch MCD from the Start Menu / Program Files menu, then load the workflow from the UI there, then the component would return the directory for the MCD installation. 

Subodh also reported that if he converted that VBScript component to a PACZ and hosted it in MCRE, then the string reports the installation directory for MCRE, not the analyses path location of the pacz file.

Is the above behavior a bug, or not? I feel that it is; ModelCenter should switch the working directory to that of the currently loaded workflow regardless of how that workflow was loaded - and at the very least, having the behavior go one way sometimes and another other times leads to inconsistent behavior. Alternatively, adding back some of the functions that used to be present to access the MCD process / object via the API would work too, if they provided consistent results. 

I've attached a much simpler example of the customer's workflow, that just has the one VBScript component, that I used to reproduce the behavior.

title: AFT: Mesh workflow : Valeo: Failed at 2nd extrusion of top surface ( face used as starting geometry)
Monitor value affected by number of cores with LiveGX CPU solver
description:
The attached very simple model shows a dependence of a heat flux monitor on the number of cores on which the LiveGX CPU solver is run.  The heat flow is predominantly in the X direction, from a high to a low temperature face, and the geometry is rectangular and so it will probably show up differences.  That is why I have given the bug a medium priority.  There is a monitor for average heat flux, Avg. Heat Flux 1, on the low temperature face.  There is also a monitor on the solid thermal body for the heat flux in the X direction, Avg. X Heat Flux 2.

When the simulation is run on 1 core, the monitor for heat flux on the face has a similar value to the value in its details plot and the value on the body (Fig. 1).

When it runs on 4 cores, the value of the heat flux on the face is quite significantly lower than the details plot and the monitor on the body (Fig.2).

The default for LiveGX CPU is 4 cores.

In both cases energy is converged to about 2.4e-08.

The issue is also seen in v251 SP1 but not in V242 SP1.

Fig. 1:  LiveGX CPU on 1 core - Monitor value for Avg. Heat Flux 1 agrees with the details plot and is similar to Avg. X Heat Flux 2 on the body



Fig. 2:  LiveGX CPU on 4 cores - Monitor value for Avg. Heat Flux 1 (3.36e4 W/m^2) is lower than the last value in the details plot (4.03e4 W/m^2) and than Avg. X Heat Flux 2 on the body

title: Custom Verilog-A component doesn't extrapolate in HB simulation
description:
I am trying to make an "Ansys only" workflow out of a similar workflow I used before I joined Ansys. There, we used HFSS + Keysight ADS for the HB simulation and ADS's SDD (Symbolically Defined Device) component. I found out that Verilog-A can be used to make an equivalent of such an SDD component in Ansys Circuit, so I created one ("0_Verilog_component_only"). It is a voltage-dependent resistor and capacitor connected in parallel, with C(U) and R(U) values taken from a lookup table. The last U value from the lookup table is around 5.5V. When a voltage source is swept at 13.56MHz in "0_Verilog_component_only," it can extrapolate the C and R values beyond 5.5V. But if a port (with 50ohm termination) is used instead, the HB simulation fails.

When an S-parameter block from HFSS, along with some lumped elements, is connected to the Verilog-A component ("1_Dynamic_link"), the HB simulation fails as soon as the input voltage to the entire system (at PCD port) exceeds the value corresponding to 5.5V at the Verilog-A component (around 14.52V). Extrapolation is not possible, and the entire HB simulation fails. @Tony Donisi and I tried changing some HB settings, but to no avail. If passivity on the dynamic link is enforced (IFPV), AEDT crashes. Due to the large archive (7.5GB), I cannot upload it with solutions, but you can try to reproduce the crash if you simulate on your side (or let me know how to provide the solved project).

Since the DC point seems problematic, I exported the S-matrix from HFSS and manually deleted the DC point, then imported that SnP into Circuit ("2_SnP_no_DC_point"). Enforcing passivity doesn't make AEDT crash here, but extrapolation is still impossible and HB simulation again fails.

Please look into this, as it is an important topic for a customer (IFX) and could potentially displace their workflow with ADS (which can extrapolate the C and R values). Thank you very much in advance.

title: Geometry import in 2023R2 VS Geometry import in 2025R1 (Rhino file format)
description:
Hello,
 
A customer has encountered issues when importing a Rhino geometry file into Spaceclaim 2025 R1 or Discovery.
 
To provide an overview, when using the ACIS kernel in older versions of Spaceclaim (which was the default), no issues were found after checking the geometry. title: ModelCenter 25R2 RC Foxtrot: MSC Nastran QuickWrap throws misleading error when output file is missing
description:
In the scenario where you have licensing for MSC Nastran configured incorrectly, upon running your component, you will not get an output file to parse as expected, because the software did not run correctly in order to generate it. This is the error message you get though:

Failed Component: Model.MSC_Nastran

An asynchronous operation completed with an error. Type: Phoenix.OutOfProcessComponentHosting.RemoteHarnessExecutionException Message: com.phoenix_int.aserver.util.scriptwrapper.PHXScriptWrapperException: Error Running ScriptWrapper
Line: 90
Source: "   caeOutstress3p_op2.parse();"
Reason: com.phoenix_int.cae.ParsingException: com.vki.VKIException: An operation failed in current state
Library not opened

I feel that it is "misleading" to the user, or at the least feels like leading them with a red herring, to have a "Library not opened" error compared to a "missing file" sort of error message. 


For what it's worth, I tried the same setup in MCD 25R1, and the error message was the same. It's probably been around for a while.

  • What happened?: When MSC Nastran licensing is configured incorrectly, running the component does not generate the expected output file. Instead, the user receives a misleading error message indicating "Library not opened" rather than a "missing file" error.
  • What should have happened?: The error message should clearly indicate that the output file is missing due to incorrect licensing configuration (or at least acknowledge that it is missing).
  • Where does it occur?: MSC Nastran component in ModelCenter Desktop v25R1 and v25R2.
  • How often does it occur?: Always, when licensing is configured incorrectly, or when there's some other sort of failure that results in the output file not being generated.


Repro Steps:

  1. Configure MSC Nastran licensing incorrectly.
  2. Run the MSC Nastran component.
  3. Observe the error message: "Failed Component: Model.MSC_Nastran An asynchronous operation completed with an error. Type: Phoenix.OutOfProcessComponentHosting.RemoteHarnessExecutionException Message: com.phoenix_int.aserver.util.scriptwrapper.PHXScriptWrapperException: Error Running ScriptWrapper Line: 90 Source: 'caeOutstress3p_op2.parse();' Reason: com.phoenix_int.cae.ParsingException: com.vki.VKIException: An operation failed in current state Library not opened."


Environment Details:

  • OS version: All Windows
  • Application version/build number: ModelCenter Desktop v25R1 and v25R2

Expected vs. Actual Behavior:

  • Expected Behavior: The error message should indicate that the output file is missing due to incorrect licensing configuration (or at least acknowledge that it is missing).
  • Actual Behavior: The error message indicates "Library not opened," which is misleading.




As a comparison, here is the error message I get in 25R2 when I try to parse a non-existing ASCII text file:


Failed Component: Model.MSC_Nastran

An asynchronous operation completed with an error. Type: Phoenix.OutOfProcessComponentHosting.RemoteHarnessExecutionException Message: com.phoenix_int.aserver.util.scriptwrapper.PHXScriptWrapperException: Error Running ScriptWrapper
Line: 111
Source: "   rowFieldOuttest_out_txt.parse();"
Reason: java.io.FileNotFoundException: C:\Users\tester\Desktop\MSC Nastran\61c289ec-a1af-4759-a8f5-e7a9e18fbc1f\test.out.txt (The system cannot find the file specified)

title: ThermalAdaptor move/copy issues
description:
We've had issues recently and prior where customers seem to not have the Thermal Ribbon installed in Spaceclaim after installing TD. To me it seems this is most likely caused by users not running as admin, but there are other issues as well. I'll layout some of what I've seen.

As far as I understand, in the TD installer, somewhere in there it runs the ThermalAdaptor.bat file, which tries to delete old versions of the Thermal Adaptor from the legacy location (C:\ProgramData) and then finally creates a CRTech directory in v242\scdm\Addins, which it gets to by navigative up a few levels from the TD install location and then moves the ThermalAdaptor folder from TD install directory to the Addins\CRTech folder. I think when customers don't use admin rights to install, either the directory creation doesn't work or the move command doesn't work and in the end they don't have the Thermal Ribbon and the ThermalAdaptor folder will remain in the ThermalDesktop install location.

Would you be able to test whether this actually occurs when installing Thermal Desktop as non-admin?

The other thing that I have encountered is users that install TD in locations other than C:\Program Files, for example a user today needed to install TD on their user account because they didn't have admin rights. He still had issue with the ThermalAdaptor and had to manually copy (or he could have run the batch script I think).

This would be another good thing to test, see what happens when TD is installed on a user account vs C:

Happy to chat more about this if you have questions.

title: Ocean load at non-zero plane causes incorrect internal pressure
description:
As part of a project for Wood Group I'm helping them move to from 16/8's to 288's etc.   There current modelling practice is to model the mudline at 0 in Z - i.e. sitting on the XY plane. 

As such I've been testing a model to understand the use of the Ocean loading to define External pressure and the use of the internal fluid density.    In my test model I simply have a line of 288's on the sea floor running in X.   For the purposes of test the internal density is set to be different that if the external sea water such that I know the right density is being used. 

I also set the pipe density to zero just for checking the reactions.  

I do not define face 1 and face 2 loads.    

I set the value of face 3 to be free surface location

Sea Depth is 100m.  

As such expected Rho-g-h loading should be 

Internal=768.75*9.81*100=754140
External = 1025*9.81*100=1000525


 From Ocdata command if the mean sea level is not a 0 then Zms1 should be used.

So with a mudline following on OCADATA
Depth=100
zmsl=100

Also for pressures - 

SFE Face 3 = 100

I get the following reported pressures via smisc, 61 and 62

Internal = 1508300 - i.e double
External =  100525

Change zmsl to zero and I get 

Internal = 754140
External = 0 

To my mind this is a defect.   

If set the mudloor to be -100 and leave zmsl to zero it works fine.   

Likewise if I don't define the ocean I get the correct internal pressure based on the Z value on face 3.   In that case I manually define the external pressure via face 2.  

My workaround for the project will to set the mean sea level at zero and have the pipeline on the sea bed at -Z to work with the Ocean loading

I'm attaching my test model.  It is set with zloc (on line 22) at zero and zmsl at 100 (line 53) and Ocean loading is included.  Set skip=1 on line 49 to remove ocean loading

Please advise.

Thanks

Mark Leddin

title: Validity of electrical simulation with a suppressed body depends on component structure
description:
Not new in v261.  Also seen in v252.

The detection of contacts for an electrical simulation appears to be less straightforward than for thermal or structural simulations.

The attached two projects saved in v252 that contain models derived from the mixer tee example simulation.  The component structures of the model differ.
  • MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco - fluid body and pipe bodies are contained in components at the same level (Fig.1)
  • MixerTee_Geom_V252.5.dsco - pipe bodies at top level and fluid body in a component (Fig. 2)
If an electrical simulation is set up on the pipe bodies with the fluid body suppressed, the simulation based on MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco is in the Cannot solve state with an error message, Unconnected bodies located as in Fig. 3.  A similar simulation based on MixerTee_Geom_V252.5.dsco, however, is valid (Fig. 4).

The animation shown in Fig. 5 shows that if physics auto update is disabled for the invalid simulation based on MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco, the simulation state changes to valid although the message is still displayed.  Moreover, the simulation can be solved and the solution appears to be similar to that obtained from the valid simulation based on MixerTee_Geom_V252.5.dsco (Figs 6 and 7).

If the fluid body in MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco is deleted, the simulation is valid and can be solved giving a solution similar to those obtained from the other set-ups.

In addition to the projects, I have attached zipped working directories for setting up the simulations on the two models with the fluid body suppressed and MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco with the fluid body deleted.

Fig. 1:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco


Fig. 2:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.5.dsco


Fig. 3:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body. Error message about unconnected bodies


Fig. 4:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.5.dsco - set up with suppressed body. Simulation is valid


Fig. 5:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body followed by switching off physics auto update


Fig. 6:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco - set up with suppressed fluid body with physics auto update disabled can be solved


Fig. 7:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.5.dsco - set up with suppressed body.  Solution is as for MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco with auto update disabled



Fig. 8:  MixerTee_Geom_V252.4.dsco - set up with fluid body deleted - no messages and solution similar to previous

title: Improving Error Handling: Targeting Specific Exceptions
description:
DESCRIPTION:
The objectif is to improve error message handling by intercepting more specific exceptions

Data:
  • \\vlbfs1\Data Repository\Incident Reports\VSS\Bug 1177603 VSS - Camera Ground Truth with Fisheye camera error message displayed is incorrect
Notes:
This situation directly impacts our ability to improve logging (Example: bug 1177603)
  • Exceptions used in component APIs (not product APIs) generally follow C# framework guidelines (ArgumentException, OutOfRangeException, OperationException, etc.), with occasional use of custom exceptions in specific cases.
  • There is no clearly defined or structured architectural approach to error handling across components.

Steps to reproduce for VSS :

  • Set the log level of VSS and VSSSpawner to INFO
  • Launch provided scenario with VssTester
    ./VRXPERIENCE.SensorsSimulator -p 5050
    Imagine.Pre.VssTester -p 5050 -s Scenario.json
  • The error message generated is not clear on what the error is, from a customer point of view, the cause of the error is not given here and cannot be understood. 
  • 2024-11-27 10:40:13,620 [18] ERROR SupervisionActivity-CreateAbortedMessage()  Failure detected on ISensorActivity<ICameraSensorService> located at {localhost:13001}: An error occurred while creating sensor. Couldn't create camera sensor with id 'cam3_fisheye'.
    2024-11-27 10:40:13,636 [18] ERROR SimulationInterfaceActivity-MoveNext()  Failure detected on ISensorActivity<ICameraSensorService>. Closing simulation interface server...
    2024-11-27 10:40:13,639 [18] ERROR SimulationCommandRpcService-MoveNext()  LoadCommand encountered an error.
  • If you change the log level to ALL you get the real error underneath which is "Camera Ground Truth production is not available for Fisheye camera."
    That error is clearer, the simulation parameter defined for the sensor are not available.
    The user is aware the parameter are incorrect and not wondering why the sensor couldn't be created.

The objective is to improve error handling by capturing more specific exceptions, so that we can address the issue and fix the bug.

Expected behavior:

  • For the current product bug : VSS can retrieve the root cause of the error :   "Camera Ground Truth production is not available for Fisheye camera."
  • For the future : 
    • A clear list of exception types used in component API.
    • Alignment on a shared strategy for error/exception

Reproducible (always, never, often, sometimes): 
always

title: GPU solver: Time-averaged Cumulative plot issue on porous zone
description:
Issue:

During an Enterprise D&A project with my customer, I observed an unrealistic result on Fluent 25R1 GPU solver.

When I plotted the cumulative drag force coefficient (Cd) from the force statistics, the force applied to the porous zone was NOT included in the plot.


Attached comparison shows that:

1.  Instantaneous cumulative Cd on the porous zone was correctly calculated. Therefore, the issue happens only when plotting from force statistics.

2.  The issue is specific to GPU solver. Not CPU solver.


To reproduce the issue:

1. Open “GPU.cas.h5” using 25R1 GPU solver

2. Initialize

3. Run for 50 timesteps and plot the “cumulative-plot-1” with checking “Compute from Force Statistics”

4. Do the same procedure for “CPU.cas.h5” using 25R1 CPU solver to make sure that CPU solver does not have the issue

In case you want to see the result without calculation, I have attached corresponding data files for each case.


@Eijiro Suzuki

title: Parasolid Error with Equation-Based Curve
description:
I’m having trouble joining an equation curve with a line to make a surface. I’m able to get this to work for certain geometries, but still see get error messages even when the modeler is able to successfully render them.


The attached file can be used to illustrate my issue. I closed both the lower and upper curves with polylines between the endpoints using “connect” operations. The surfaces render. If I change certain parameters that affect the upper curve, I see “CoverLine operation failed.”


As an example, please change Ri (flare rate) from 0.5 to 0.55, and you will see the error, but the surface still renders. 


With Ri set to 0.55, change element_w to 5.9, and you will see that the surface fails to render. 


Change element_w back to 5.8 and the surface appears again, but we get the “CoverLine operation failed” error again.

title: Perturbation in moment calculated from Rolling Resistance Type C Model while passing boundary triangles
description:
Lucas from CADFEM shared two test cases and one PDF summarising their findings. They are attached to this ticket: "rolling resistance.pdf" and "528872_rolling_resistance.zip". The first test case is with finer boundary mesh, where they found the issue. Then, they tested with the coarse mesh version and the issue was not observed. The force value was at the expected value. I ran these cases as well and confirmed the issue.

Then, I modified the coarse mesh case and created a version with a single particle only (attached as "Rollreibung_coarseMesh_rollTypeC_1particle.rocky_archive"). I increased the simulation time from 1 s to 2 s and modified the motion frames accordingly. I did this test to see what happens in the coarse mesh case when the particle crosses the triangle boundary. This showed that actually the force is at the expected value until the particle crosses the boundary. Then it starts diverging from this value while it is passing it. Please see the plot below, where this issue can be seen after t~1.7 s.

title: Specify Total Voltage option in Electrolysis is not working properly
description:
@Chao Han cc @Omkar Champhekar @Anil Wakale @Saurabh Patwardhan 

Hello Chao,

I worked with a client's PEMWE model with a dry cathode and attempted to run it for U=1.8V from the initialization file. It took me a little while to set up all the monitors and plots that I typically use. I run it overnight and it is going in the right direction and I am confident that I can converge it even better. 

The mass balance between the water consumed and total mass of gases generated, is getting closer but fluctuate a bit. I will experiment with the pseudo-transient time stepping strategy for solution steering to find out whether a better steady-state convergence can be reached, or whether we are dealing with a larger time-scale transience somewhere in PTLs or PTL/channel regions or elsewhere. This might as well be the case.

Having said that, I noticed an issue with the model. Typically, I monitor the volume integrals of transfer currents in the catalysts and they match up well.
At the same time, I monitor the surface integrals of the wall-normal current density component at terminals. To my surprise they failed to match
Please disregard the units difference between the last two plots. The transfer current integrals were in [A/(m3) * m3] whereas the last plot has inconsistency of units [A/(cm2) * m2]. I am more concerned about the difference of currents on terminals as shown in the last plot. The conservation of charge should be satisfied and I started searching for a leak, given that convergence was not perfect but it was on the right track. 

To discover this, I plotted the current density plots on all outer surfaces. Please see results below:


The flange side of the catalyst is the place where the leak takes place, but the boundary conditions are greyed out, because the voltage was specified in the electrolysis panel.
A similar situation is observed on the other side:
At the same time, this should not be the case, because the voltage and the terminals are specified in the Potential/Electrochemistry Electrolysis panel:


This looks like a juicy bug to me. I will use the workaround for the time being but it feels that it is important to find the source of this bug as it can resurface unexpectedly on bigger, more complex geometries and remain unnoticed for a long time.

I will share the files via the secure file transfer facility.

Kind regards,
Aleksey.

  • The STK Model Center plugin now attempts to store the STK scenario location as a relative path so that you can zip the model center workspace and move it to a different location without having to relocate the STK scenario at startup after moving. This feature will work when the STK scenario is stored under the Model Center workspace location path.
  • The Model Center user can modify the scenario associated with an STK Processing block in a Model Center model. STK will load the updated scenario when it executes the processing block. You should make changes to the STK scenario from within Model Center by using the Configure STK processing block method, to ensure passing consistency checks performed during configuration. title: Feedback Iterator is buggy
description:
The feedback iterator seems buggy. In the properties, the "Latest Delta Temperature %" does not get printed until all iterations are done, and even then it only gets printed if the value is less than the "Target Delta Temperature %." If it reaches the max iterations and the value is internally greater, then it still prints "not available."
Also "Results > Clean up solutions" in Maxwell sometimes sets the "Iterations" Completed" back to zero and sometimes it does not. It's random so hard to produce, but try it 3 times or so. If it fails, and you try to update the feedback iterator when the iterations completed are at the "Max Iterations" then you'll get an error. The only way to solve this is to delete/recreate the feedback iterator and link again to the setup cell of the Maxwell system.
Also, Mechanical reports the following error if open during the feedback iterator updates, even when the iterations seem to work properly:
"One or more files from the upstream system are missing. The files may not have been copied over or saved with the project."
So it's best to close Mechanical during the iterations to avoid the error.
___________________________________________________________________________
There are no graceful exits. Mechanical crashes easy.
1. If you have cut out the bodies from the vacuum enclosure in Maxwell, this is not proper setup and will crash Mechanical, when using the feedback iterator, with no useful error.
2. If a body for temperature feedback in Mechanical is not meshed with pure tetrahedrals, it crashes Mechanical. This is probably something that just needs to be added to documentation, unless it's not intended to work this way, in which case, it needs fixing.

In both cases above Mechanical solves but crashed at the point of sending data back to Maxwell. The crash will not happen if turn off "export after solve" on the imported load folder. There will be a "ExportDiagnostics_###_####.dat" file in the solution directory meant for error reporting but it's useless because it just has one line when the export fails and when it works it just reports number of cores and export time.
See attached model, but it's just a simple model to work with to repeat the problems above. It's not unique in any way to demonstrate the problems.

Require a complete review and validation of the physics in section "Give particles specifications" and how the scattering variation is defined in the material editor:

  1. In the UG the Diffusion coefficient is the inverse of the mean free path : σd=1/ｌ with ｌ being the mean free path.


  • In literature the scattering coefficient is defined as the probability of a photon being scattered per unit path length. Therefore, what the UG labels as the "diffusion coefficient" is, by standard definition, the scattering coefficient.
  • In literature the diffusion coefficient (D) is defined as (Section 2.3):
  • μa​ (absorption coefficient) and μs′​ (reduced scattering coefficient) both have units of m−1. Therefore the denominator has units of m−1 and therefore D the unit m.

  3. Customer would like an answer how the term "diffusion coefficient" is defined in SPEOS in relation to the material properties and to what extent the scattering coefficient is taken into account.
  4. Customer would like a clarification whether the diffusion coefficient in the UG and Speos material definition actually refers to the scattering coefficient or the reduced scattering coefficient?

  5. Minor enhancements: The symbol choice σd​ is unusual and confusing for the customer. Standard notation is:

    • μa​ = absorption coefficient

    • μs​ = scattering coefficient

    • μt​=μa​+μs​ = total attenuation coefficient

title: Default Mesh for IE/Hybrid Dipole More Than 15x Slower to Run Than Common Sense Settings, 10x Slower than FEM with Defaults
description:
This submission might be an enhancement request, but I am submitting as a defect because the default meshing for a simple dipole using the IE/hybrid solver is unacceptable from both an efficiency and consistency perspective.

The IE/hybrid solved dipole with default mesh settings is 15 times slower than an IE/hybrid  mesh that uses common sense mesh settings, and over 10 times slower than the same model run in FEM.  A dipole is one of the simplest and most likely test models for a user to attempt using AEDT.  However, most users never plot mesh or have a concept of what an appropriate mesh should be, so will accept the very unnecessary slow simulation time as an HFSS metric that makes our IE/hybrid solve capabilities look bad compared to other tools.

The MoM type solvers in AEDT (IE, Q3D ACRL, etc.) have significantly different mesh requirements than FEM.  MoM is MUCH more sensitive to mesh quality (aspect ratio) and element count than FEM.  

In the attached project, IE_Dipole_2025R2.aedt, there are three IE designs (1, 2, and 3).  From left to right we have:
  1. Z oriented dipole with default mesh settings (IE)
  2. Y oriented dipole with default mesh settings (IE)
  3. Z oriented dipole with Classic mesher and 6 sided mesh due to manual mesh settings (IE)


The design summary demonstrates an extreme difference between the final mesh and solve time for the default settings and the model with custom mesh settings.  What should take 32 seconds (design 3) takes 8min13sec (design 1) with default mesh settings.

IE Designs  (mesh count and solve times are up to 15x different, and default settings yield over order of magnitude worse performance)
Design Name                                 Dipole Orientation           Initial Mesh    Passes      Final Mesh   Solve Time    Slowdown
1_IE_DefaultMesh_Z                                    Z                                 7944                 3               13426             8:13          15.4x
2_IE_DefaultMesh_Y                                    Y                                 2514                 2                3268              1:57          3.7x
3_IE_CustomMesh_Z                                  Z (mesh ops)                744                  2                  968              0:32          reference


Also, in the attached project there are three FEM designs (4, 5, and 6) that replicate the setup of the IE designs, but solving as FEM.  From left to right we have:
4. Z oriented dipole with default mesh settings (FEM)
5. Y oriented dipole with default mesh settings (FEM)
6. Z oriented dipole with Classic mesher and 6 sided mesh due to manual mesh settings (FEM)


The FEM design summary demonstrates that for exactly the same setup as designs 1-3, but solving in FEM, the mesh count and solve time is almost the same regardless of default mesh, orientation, or with the custom mesh.  
FEM Designs  (all mesh counts and solve times are similar)
Design Name                                 Dipole Orientation           Initial Mesh    Passes      Final Mesh   Solve Time    
4_FEM_DefaultMesh_Z                          Z                                 3244                  4              6976               0:40
5_FEM_DefaultMesh_Y                          Y                                 4733                  3              7581               0:34
6_FEM_CustomMesh_Z                         Z (mesh ops)              2273                  6              7435               0:46

In summary:
*Among the IE/hybrid designs, a dipole takes 15.4x to 3.7x longer to run with default settings than with the common sense custom mesh settings (6 sided cylinder).  
*An IE/hybrid vertical dipole is more than 10x slower than the same FEM dipole when both use default mesh settings.
*The IE/hybrid model with common sense mesh settings has a faster solve time compared to all of the FEM designs
*FEM solve statistics are approximately the same with either default or custom mesh (6 sided cylinder) settings.

The goal of this submission is to improve the default mesh for IE/hybrid such that it does not create high aspect ratio, inconsistent, inefficient meshes.  A simple cylinder is not representative of the range of geometries we see, but there should be more intelligence in the IE/hybrid mesher to avoid defaults yielding >10x speed penalties, and for the behavior to be so dependent on orientation.

title: 'General Error' with Layered Section scoping when body's Material field is undefined
description:
The issue was reported by a customer for release 2025R2. I've attached a demo Project where the issue is shown.

Assume a Surface body with no definition of Thickness or Material.



When we scope a Layered Section object to the Surface's body, we cannot proceed with the solution and the Thickness field is highlighted indicating that an input of a thickness value is required prior to Layered Section Scoping.



To fix this, a random thickness value is specified, and the Layered Section is re-scoped.





When proceeding with the solution, we get a 'general error'.



Looking into the ds.dat it seems that the Materials are never sent to the Solver.



To fix this, a random Material is assigned to the Surface body prior to the Layered Section scoping, similar to how it was done for the Thickness field.

The Thickness and Material definition requirements for the Layered Section scoping aren't written anywhere in the documentation. I would suggest this information is included so that users know about it. If it's possible to also highlight the Material field in Mechanical if it's undefined - similar to how it's done for the Thickness - that'd be great.

Thanks!

title: Twin Builder: Delay Block Parameters
description:
In Twin Builder (2025R1) when using a Delay block (found under Basic Elements->Blocks->Discrete Blocks->DELAY) the main input parameters, Delay Time and Samples only allow numeric input. No variables allowed, as can be seen in the screenshot below. So, my first question is: #1 Why can the Delay block not accept variables as parameter inputs, and can this capability be added or is it a fundamental limitation?



Now for the strange behavior. I was able to enter variables into the TS (sample time) and Samples parameters via the Properties window. As shown in the screenshot below. The program did not have an issue with this, and now when the parameters window was opened it would simply show “0” for the Delay Time but Samples would be reset to “20” which is the default value. When run, the Delay block will correctly utilize the variables entered for TS via the Properties window (using variables), however anything entered for Samples will be ignored and run with the default value of 20.


So, as long as I was ok with a sample number of 20, I could parameterize the delay time with a variable, and this variable could even be dynamic throughout the simulation. See below a plot where the sample time TS was set using variables as a function of time so the delay grows throughout the simulation as can be seen by the phase/frequency shift. This indicates that there is no fundamental limitation to using variables and even dynamic variables. However the experience entering parameter values via the Properties window is certainly buggy. So my question #2 Can anyone explain this observed behavior or is this a bug?

title: Issue with overlap of contacts and fluid-solid interface in Simulation 2
description:
The attached project contains 2 similar thermal simulations, as illustrated in Fig. 1.  The bodies in the FuseOnBoard... component have been imprinted to ensure 1 to connections.

If a fluid wall condition is added to the enclosure body in Simulation 1, there is only one SID message and it is an informational message suggesting that buoyancy be switched on (Fig. 2).

A workaround is to suppress and then unsuppress the solid thermal bodies (note that one of the bodies in the Fuse component is suppressed in the CHT simulation).

Fig. 1:  Thermal simulation set-up



Fig. 2:  Fluid wall applied to enclosure in Simulation 1 - no message about overlaps

title: Fluent and External Model cannot properly read/interpret the named surface element sets from Abaqus
description:
The attached Abaqus file consists of a rectangular, hexahedral mesh with faces named: UP DOWN FRONT BACK RIGHT LEFT. When the attached Abaqus file is read into Fluent, the surfaces are all lumped into a wall region called "default-exterior-1"

If the same file is read into the External model cell in Workbench and then hooked up to MEchanical, the mesh and all its surface named selections can be viewed.



This mesh cannot be exported via File> Export, however.  The export fails with an overlapping Named selections error:


Trying to fix the Named Selections does not help, which I assume means that there is some problem interpreting them.

ICEMCFD shows no surface elements when the mesh is read in, so it is possible that these cannot be read by the translator at all.  The result is that customers currently have no way to completely transfer their Abaqus meshes to Fluent.

This issue seems to affect all relatively recent releases of Fluent.  (I tried v2020 and the result is the same)

title: Time average of custom property seems off
description:
Please refer to "Problem 2" reported by CADFEM on the attached PPT for complete analysis.

On my end, I have conducted a similar analysis, and this is my reasoning:

The ShearAvgSPH custom property is created on SPH:
ShearAvgSPH: sum(A[1:t+1])/(t*OUTPUT_FREQUENCY) where A is Shear Stress

This is a time-averaged shear stress. So, if plotted on an inspector, it should be the actual Shear Stress from the inspector, since it is a single element/value. We should at least see this with a similar magnitude as the Shear Stress grid function, but in fact we don't:



Also, note that strangely, the time-averaged property is only available until 4.11 s instead of 5 s.

Our channel partner is reporting a bug in the behaviour of value2string callback.

 

Using the value2string callback with the control attribute set to float, the internal property value replaces whatever string the callback returns before the first white space in the returned string since 2025R2. See screenshot below:


The Channel Partner has provided a demo ACT extension attached (in value2string_bug.zip). To reproduce this behaviour, add the demo extension to workbench. Then, under the environment object in the model tree, RMB > Insert the sample object created by the extension and review the Float Value field.

The CP noted that if control attribute is set to double, value2string works correctly in the example.

They mentioned that Ansys examples use both float and double and that allowed values are not documented.

 

Can someone investigate this further?

title: modelon needs to generate a better error message for error found in d1221132
description:
this is from d1221132 to have modelon generate a better error message when a parameter is assigned a value in a function. from modelon:
"It is a problem in the model, on line 530 there is an assign statement that looks like this: index := i;. The variable index is a parameter in the function, it is not allowed to assign parameters in the algorithm. The parameter is declared on line 524 and looks like this: parameter Integer i,kk, index=0;.
If you replace the declaration with the following the model will compile: Integer index=0;. (There is no need to declare i and kk, they are automatically declared by the for-loops.)"

In 2025R1, an option to import empty components was added.
When the option was turned off, it was in the state of 2023R2 to 2024R1
When the option was turned on, it was in the state of 2024R2
So it was not in the state before 2023R1.

title: [AMPP] Plots don't switch to dark theme
description:
Plots in AMPP don't switch to dark theme when the dark theme is selected. Currently angular-plotly.js does not support the standard plotly themes, https://github.com/plotly/angular-plotly.js/issues/157. Once this is addressed, the layout.template field can be set to "plotly" for the light theme or "plotly_dark" for the dark theme.

Predefined plotly theme values: 
"plotly", "plotly_white", "plotly_dark", "ggplot2", "seaborn", "simple_white", "none"
Another option would be to set plot background and trace colors whenever the theme changes. This could get a bit involved.

title: Values for laminate layers change after import and editing
description:
After importing a stackup, the values for some laminate layers are not set properly.
After editing and saving the layer without changing any values, the values are changed in the stackup table.

Steps
  1. In order to start from a clean state, delete the laminate.csv file in Sherlock settings, located at C:\Users\<user name>\AppData\Roaming\Sherlock.
  2. Launch Sherlock.
  3. Enable the "Laminate Resin" Beta Feature.
  4. Import the Tutorial Project.
  5. Open the Laminate Manager.
  6. Import the attached laminate files (LaminateExport_EM-892K.csv and LaminateExport_MC24P.csv). Note that this can be done prior to importing the project.
  7. View the Stackup. Import the attached stackup file (46L Stackup.csv)
  8. Laminate layers 72, 76, 80, and 84. Note the values for layer 72:
    1. CTExy=14.000
    2. CTEz=60.000
    3. Exy=24.804
    4. Ez=6634
  9. Note the values for the stackup:
    1. CTExy=24.472
    2. CTEz=69.382
    3. Exy=25491
    4. Ez=5785
  10. Edit layer 72. The Laminate Material may be set to OAK-MITSUI, POLYMIDE, MC24P. If it isn't, change it to this. Save changes.
Results
  1. Note the values for layer 72 changed to the following (which happens regardless of whether the material was set):
    1. CTExy=24.000
    2. CTEz=25.000
    3. Exy=2000
    4. Ez=2000
    5. Material name does not change for the row if it wasn't changed from importing the OAK-MITUI material.
  2. Note the values for the stackup changed to the following:
    1. CTExy=24.602
    2. CTEz=68.843
    3. Exy=25525
    4. Ez=5703
There is now an Errors tab at the bottom of the Stackup tab.
The error is: 
Unknown Material name Elite Materials (EMC) FR-4 EM-892K RESIN, using DEFAULT
Similar behavior is seen if the stackup is imported prior to importing the laminate file LaminateExport_MC24P.csv. Sometimes when doing it in this order, the material for these laminate layers get set when importing the laminate.

Expected
The laminate material is always set in the stackup layer in the table and the layer editor after importing the missing laminate material. This is inconsistent and I haven't found a consistent way to get the values to be set.
These values would be set automatically when the stackup is imported.
There would not be an error.
Importing the stackup again after this doesn't change anything.

title: CADFEM claims that mechdat imports increase their import time in new releases
description:
CADFEM on behalf of customer ROBERT BOSCH claims the following about mechdat imports.
This is customer original message. After this a long thread was created and treated by Jogesh Chopra.

Thread is attached below.
  • Case Number: 00119054
  • Customer Account Number: {0083574
  • Customer Account: 200325
  • Customer User:   Susanne Haase
  • Subject: performance of mechdat import
  • Description: 

    Hi, this is a service request for Dirk Haverkamp, Robert Bosch GmbH.

    In our automation project for Bosch a lot of mechdats get imported and assembled by script. The more parts we assemble, the worse the performance of the project schematic gets. What can we do, to improve the performance?

    Attached you will find a test script and a test mechdat. You have to adjust the path in line 71+118. For the first run I would recommend to keep n=5. A typical number of mechdats is n=200.

    What we observed so far is, that it has a main impact, on which maschine we start the process. On my laptop it takes 3h, but at Bosch it is up to 6h for the import of 200 mechdats. title: Part density is not calculated correctly in Sherlock
description:
To reproduce this defect, enable "Use Part Body Weight" advanced setting. For SQUARE, ROUND, and MITER corner shape, the same density value is used because it is based off the part weight value set. But, since the corner being cutoff will change the volume/mass, it should be using a different density value if the volume/mass is different. When exported to Mechanical, you can see this difference in the mass of the component being less than the specified weight. But in the ds.dat, you can see that they all use the same density value because they have the same material assigned that all use the same part weight. The component needs updated to the true weight entered or a new part density needs calculated based off the corner shape.

Hi,

I have manually defined part weight for a component. When I exported the model to Mechanical, it shows a different value than what was defined in Sherlock. 

Upon further testing, I realized that it is happening when the corner shape is not square.

Could you please check this?

title: Vias missing when importing IPC-2581 in SIwave
description:
Vias missing when importing IPC-2581 in SIwave

Attached is an .xml file that comes from an IPC export from Altium. When importing into SIwave, some vias are missing. These vias are not missing when importing in HFSS 3D Layout, thus confirming that the issue is not with the Altium export, but the SIwave import.

First, to see the correct import in HFSS:
1. Import the IPC file in HFSS 3D Layout 25R1.
2. From List, find the component with name C83CV0CG0 and fit in the screen
3. Perform a cutout around this component (include and clip all nets)
4. It is visible that the vias go from top to bottom:



Now to see the wrong import in SIwave:
1. Import the IPC file in SIwave 25R1
2. Using Find Components, search for component named C83CV0CG0 and fit the screen to it
4. Perform a cutout around this component
5. Rotate so that the Z axis is visible. It is easily shown that the vias are not reaching all the way from top to bottom:


Since SIwave has some visualization issues when rotating, you can export to HFSS 3D Layout and check that this is true there also.

Attached are also zipped versions of the HFSS and SIwave imports.

title: Loading SolveHandlers.xml from Appdata may fail when multiple instances of mechanical are interacting with the file
description:
This is a follow-up on recent cert failure for QK_CIT_BUILD1_07. The test was intermittently failing due to a timing issue regarding SolveHandlers.xml file.

I quick fix was made with pr - PR 612078: Potential fix for cert QK_CIT_BUILD1_07 which adds handling around the exception being thrown. We need to study why this error is happening and if/how it can be fixed. Below is my email on the topic:

Regarding test QK_CIT_BUILD1_07, I have some updates.

 

After discussing with @Andrei Marinescu the status of this test, it appears it has been failing inconsistently for quite some time now all the way back to June. This ruled out any changes recently.

 

After investigating, it appears it is a timing issue when multiple instances of Mechanical are interacting with the following file in appdata at the same time (AppData\Roaming\Ansys\v261\SolveHandlers.xml)

 

I tracked the change which I believe to be the cause from a PR from June 10th addressing bug B1274889:

  • Pull request 595328: Update JobHandlerManager if xml file is updated through another session. - Repos
  • Pull request 597616: B1274889: CallScript doesn't work if method already defined in JScriptCombined - Repos (follow up)

 

I may have a temporary fix that Andrei is trying out.

 

As a resolution, I think there are two options:

  1. Revert both PR’s and re-open bug 1274889 until the root cause is investigated more thoroughly and fixed
  2. Merge the temporary fix if it is successful and open a new bug to explore a more permanent solution if necessary.

description:
When creating a domain and adding fluid definitions in CFX Pre, if the material is particle transport solid, cannot select panel items below "particle diameter change" in Dark/Light mode. This also occurs in Windows/Windows Classic, however at a lower point on the panel.

To recreate:
  1. Download and open the attached CFX file in CFX Pre with light or dark mode enabled
  2. Right click "Flow Analysis 1" and add a new domain
  3. On the Basic Settings, tab under Fluid and Particle Definitions, delete Fluid 1 and create a new fluid definition named Gas Mixture.
  4. Click Add new item and create a new fluid definition named HC Fuel.

Basic Settings Location and Type  
   
> Location B40
Fluid and Particle Definitions Gas Mixture
Fluid and Particle Definitions  
   
> Gas Mixture  
   
> Material Gas Mixture [a]
Fluid and Particle Definitions

title: Missing information on components' nodes/elems format in rst files
description:
The issue was reported by a Channel Partner.

According to the doc (1.2. Description of the Results File), in the rst file format for the COMP section, we first have the component type, then the component name, and then a list of nodes / elements of the components. However, for compression purposes, if the list of nodes / elements are in a continuous order from value A to value B, they are reported as A -B in the file format. This logic with the negative sign is not mentioned anywhere in the doc, and can lead to confusion when users try to process the rst files.

Please include this information in the doc.

title: Histogram y-axis label becomes misleading if weight is used
description:
In this example, what happens is that the frequency of the bins (i.e. their height) is weighted by Duration : Mean. The heights do not represent Duration : Mean in seconds, but rather the distribution of the particles' mean impact normal velocity weighted based on the mean contact duration of each particle.



However, the customer was misled to believe the y-values were actually in seconds, which is not plausible. Thankfully, he realized there was a 6s mean contact duration for a 5s simulation, which does not make sense, but I wonder if it could happen to a not-so-flagrant case.

Therefore, please remove this inconsistency from the y-label.

Steps to reproduce
1. Run tutorial 4
2. Take inter particle collision Duration and Impact Velocity
3. Plot impact normal velocity on a histogram
4. Use Duration : mean as weight

title: HFSS-Icepak: Excitation port shows absurdly high surface loss
description:
Customers: RTX, Northrop Grumman, Seattle, etc.

In the attached project, please only consider the HFSS design 1a_RFpcb_1way. 

After solving this design as is, the Radiation> 3D> Antenna parameters shows a total of 1 W incident. Using the field calculator, we can verify that the substrate has ~ 0.776 W volumetric load, while the antenna and the Ground copper surface loads add up to 0.155 W, which gives us a total loss of 0.931 W. So far so good.

Now, select all objects in HFSS and copy them. Then create a new Icepak design, and paste the copied geometries from HFSS here. Select all objects in Icepak, and assign an EM Loss from the above HF design. After solving, Icepak shows a total heat loss of ~ 2.78 W instead of 0.931 W. This is because an extra 1.85 W of surface loss comes in from the 2D terminal port surface in HFSS.

If you go back to the HFSS design and check with the field calculator, once can verify that the excitation port shows a total surface loss of ~ 1.85 W. This is an absurd result. Following seem problematic:
1. If the 3D> Antenna parameters only reports an incident power of 1 W, how can the port show a much higher loss.
2. Since the port is expected to have 1 W incident, why are we seeing any loss at the port at all. In this simple model, all the input power incident at the port is either useful em, or reflected, or ends up as heat losses as suggested in the 3D> Antenna parameters report. Therefore, the reported loss in the excitation port should be zero.

The only resolution seems to be to recognize the port loss as spurious and exclude it from the Icepak design. This loss seems misleading.

title: ModelCenter Desktop 25R1 BETA: Minerva component in Analysis View shows URL in properties, but when the "..." button is used, it opens a local directory
description: If you have a Minerva component in your workflow, and then look at the properties for the component, you will see the Minerva URL used.
