title: ACTDYNA Testing Interface Delamination and Contact Debonding
description:
• Interface Delamination not working when one or more penta cohesive element is required:
    Please see attached model "WBLSDYNA_Delamination_ELFORM_Testing_25R1dev.wbpz".

    In Interface Delamination Scoping exclude or include the related geometry face where penta elements are required. 

  • ACP Model with Interface layers - Contact Debonding cannot get scoped to Bonded Contact with Scoping Method Pre-Generated Interface:
    See attached model: "WBLSDYNA_Delamination_withACP_Testing_25R1dev.wbpz" System B. Suppress Interface Delamination object and unsuppress Contact Debonding object and Bonded Contact. Contact Debonding Scope does not allow scoping the Bonded Contact. 

  • Cohesive Elements not shown in Mechanical GUI:
    Could there be a way to expose them as a mesh feature. This would enable to do postprocessing on cohesive elements in Mechanical. Workaround is either LSPP or perhaps through PyAnsys environment. Can be checked with any of attached models.

  • Visualization issues of deformation plot when Cohesive Elements in a single body (ACP):
    After Cohesive Elements are failed: Deformation Plot with missing visualization on solid element face adjacent to the cohesive elements. See attached model: "WBLSDYNA_Delamination_withACP_Testing_25R1dev.wbpz"

    before cohesive element failure


    after cohesive element failure


  • Visualization issues of stress plot when Cohesive Elements in a single body (ACP):
    After Cohesive Elements are failed: Stress plot with where solid element nodes on one side of the cohesive element layer are connected to the Solid element nodes to the other side of the cohesive element layer. There should be a gap instead. See attached model: "WBLSDYNA_Delamination_withACP_Testing_25R1dev.wbpz"

    before cohesive element failure


    after cohesive element failure

  • Time History Output Controls
    when specific time history output is selected e.g. Nodal Interface Forces (NCFORC), then *DATABASE_NCFORC is present twice in the k-file. Leads to a warning when opening in LSPP. Seems all *DATABASE_ items are written when using program controlled anyway. When manually specifying shouldn't the default just removed from the k-file? Can be checked with any model.

  • Interface Layer Open Area to Pre-Meshed Crack: ACPs Interface Layers allow to define an Open Area. This translates to a Pre-Meshed Crack in Mechanical Tree. The Pre-Meshed Crack object is not valid for WB-LSDYNA whereas it is for MAPDL models. This would be rather an Enhancement request for 25R2. Motivation: This allows to define a predefined zone within plies are not connected e.g. to model a predefined defect which is common practice e.g. in aerospace to account for manufacturing defects.

title: Maxwell DCBiasedEddyCurrent solver fails if Thin Layer Conductor is defined
description:
Maxwell Eddy Current solver supports thin layer boundary conditions for conductive/high permeability materials, thus allowing shell element adoption for shielding applications.

For thin structures immersed in DC fields, like in magnetic signature applications, this feature would be of great benefit allowing to save time and resources. If Thin Layer conductor is defined in DCBiased Eddy Current solver and the solution is started, the DC part fails, probably because the magnetostatic solver does not support it.

Please find in attachment a simple example where EC solver solves successfully but DCBiasedEC solver fails.
Warm Regards,
Tiziana

title: Q3D Tau Mesh Failure
description:
The Q3D model is a 20x20 array of tall square copper posts from Istvan Novak at Samtec.  The model was created and run previously in 2024.1, but is failing in 2025.1.  

I explored all meshers in 2025.1 and 2025.2 in two separate projects that are attached.

Here is a summary of outcomes for 2025.1.  Note that the mesh Auto setting uses Classic/Phi for this model.

Version           Mesher          Outcome                           Error
2025.1         Classic/Phi        Fails for DCRL and ACRL      Insufficient Memory Error
2025.1              TAU              Fails for ACRL                      Invalid SAT file
2025.1            Prime              WORKS                               None. But high DCRL mesh aspect ratio
2025.1   Prime w/mesh op   Fails                                      Insufficient Memory Error

The "Insufficient Memory Error" error messages in 2025.1 are nonsense because the model isn't within a factor of 100 of the RAM limit, and there is no SAT geometry since it is only HFSS native box primitives from 2024.1.  The insufficient memory error seems to already be fixed in 2025.2
Here is a summary of outcomes for 2025.2 (March 7, 2025 build)

Version           Mesher          Outcome                           Error
2025.2         Classic/Phi          WORKS                              None. But high mesh aspect ratio for ACRL solve takes 80-100 iterations and makes 4x+ slower simulation than Prime
2025.2              TAU              Fails for DCRL and ACRL      Invalid SAT file
2025.2            Prime              WORKS                               None. But high DCRL mesh aspect ratio
2025.2   Prime w/mesh op    WORKS                               None.  But mesh operation seems to have length halved for ACRL mesh?

The customer plans to scale up to post arrays that have thousands of nets/objects.  2025.1 only runs with the Prime mesher and with no mesh operations.

title: UI issue in Winding definition for IM1PH
description:
There are couple of UI issues on the winding of single-phase induction motor, that one of our channel partner (DRD) customer pointed out during his Evalution of MotorCAD:
  • As you can see on the attached model (and on the image below) that the first column is missing the header name, I checked the default model, and it doesn't seem to have this issue, so I am not sure what cause this in the customer's model. Also, the Main column seems to show the number of turns for the Auxiliary winding (even in the default model). I think this can be improved by having two columns the first one for Main winding and the second one for Auxiliary winding, instead of Phase 1 and Main.   
  • Entering or modifying the coil definition on the table is not always consistent and there are several issues that I noticed, I have recorded some snaps to show some of those behavior:
  1.  The numbers change to the first entry on the table (Slot 1 Go) once you select some of cells. Once you move out of the cell, the number resets to the original value (see Number_Change.mp4) 
  2.  When you enter a number on cell and then move out without pressing Enter, sometimes it takes that entry and sometimes it doesn't, and it will reset to another number (see Number_reset_uncorrectly.mp4 and Second_time_it worked_Fine.mp4)
  3.  Sometimes even when you change the number and press enter, it doesn't work at the first try and reset the number but works at the second try.
Those issues I mentioned are not repeatable, But I would say definitely there are some inconsistencies and strange behaviors entering the information on the table, I hope there is a way to improve it to be more consistent.

title: IM Lab Link Testing - Wrong LUT values Imported from Max. to Motor-CAD
description:
The issue is related to the IM Lab Link and found during the AFT. The workflow works smoothly in all the steps of the split analysis. The problem is related to the LUT values we can see are imported into motor-CAD.

If we look at the phase inductance and magnetizing inductance, they are:

IMLookup_Phase_Inductance = [1 : 0.999999999999999 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1 : 0.999999999999999 : 1]

IMLookup_Magnetizing_Inductance = [0.999839060707254 : 0.999844713438522 : 0.999883511195053 : 0.999909157375598 : 0.999925833108243 : 0.999937496990208 : 0.999946113398189 : 0.999952693507017 : 0.99995784093144 : 0.999961959511273 : 0.999965323245343 : 0.999968117332725]

It looks that the phase inductance is not calculated properly, even though the flux linkage calculation through the FEA model in the Maxwell file appears to be correct.



The flux linkage D increases with the current correctly in the optimetrics set up by the Setup Model.



The inductance values follows a saturation pattern as expected, all different from ~1H as imported later into motor-CAD.

The consequence of this issue in Motor-CAD Lab post-processing are clearly visible. The too high inductance value makes the torque vs. speed being quite strange:



@Sufei Li , @Etienne Kaiser , please let us know the solution you're working on here, so we can track better the development.

@Daniel Bachinski , FYI

title: [PyAEDT] Run ignores interferer set on interaction domain
description:
1. Set one Rx and one Tx on an interaction domain
  2. Run that domain to get an interaction
  3. Get the worst instance from that interaction
  4. Get the domain from that worst instance
  5. Get the Tx from that domain
The Tx on the resulting domain may not match the Tx that was set before running.

This was found as part of an ACE micro-hackathon where we were attempting to write a PyAEDT script using the results API that recreates the Scenario matrix. When building the matrix, instead of getting the worst case EMI for each cell as expected when setting one Rx and one Tx, we instead always get the worst case EMI for the entire Rx row, even when setting a different Tx.  

Attached a script that reproduces the error. 
  • Run as-is to see what should be a Scenario matrix recreation showing the worst-case EMI for every Tx/Rx pair, but every cell within a row gets the same EMI. 
  • Uncomment the two commented lines inside the loop to see the assert verify the set domain and resulting domain don't match.

title: Fluent 2025 R1 uses dx11 by default and crashes when closing the Remote Desktop Connection
description:
Fluent 2025 R1 uses by default the dx11 graphic driver and causes a crash when closing the Remote Desktop if an interactive Fluent simulation is running.

 

As a workaround, change the driver by using this text command in the Fluent TUI (Text User Interface):

/display/set/rendering-options/driver/opengl2


Can you investigate why Fluent 2025 R1 on Windows uses by default dx11?


Can you also investigate why this will cause a Fluent if Fluent is runing interactively on a remote machine and the Remote Desktop Connection window is closed?

title: LSDSO: desktopjob problem with command line arguments containing commas
description:
Some of the code used by desktopjob to create ansysedt command  lines uses a comma as an argument separator. This does not work correctly if any of the command line arguments contain one or more comma characters.

I have not heard of customers experiencing this issue. I ran into it when using a local build of desktopjob. My locally built copy of desktopjob could not find the Ansys registry files, so it used the fallback for the temporary directory. On Windows, the fallback directory is a subdirectory of the OneDrive directory, which includes a comma in the pathname. The code for the fallback temporary directory calls SHGetFolderPath() to get the CSIDL_PERSONAL directory. This used to be the MyDocuments directory, but with recent Windows versions, it is the OneDrive Documents directory. On my office PC, the OneDrive folder is named "OneDrive - ANSYS, Inc". The embedded comma triggers this issue.

title: Sound pipelines - build folders numbers on DFS do not always match exe build number
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
The build number in the folder name on DFS may not match the build number of the exe contained in this folder.
The correct value is the one of the exe.

Data:

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
Run two pipelines Product simultaneously (SAS, JLT, DPF_Sound)
Once the pipelines are finished, it is very likely that some of the binaries version numbers and the version numbers used for the dfs folders or the pipeline log files are different for a same pipeline.
> build number should be the same all along a same pipeline
> two different pipeline runs should use two different build numbers

Expected behavior:
Build number in the folder name on DFS do match the build number of the exe contained in this folder

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
The stages of the different pipelines may interlace.
In the Build stage, we read and update the build number, which is the correct number in the exe properties.
In the Publish stage, we re-read this number (without modification). 
However, if a Build stage of any pipeline was run between Build and Publish, it modified again the build number, which is now wrong.

Solution:
document work-in-progress: Management of version numbers in Sound pipelines (work in progress).pptx

Store the build number inside the pipeline, to transmit it from one stage to the next one.
  1. explore the possibility to use a "pipeline variable"
  2. if 1. is not possible, maybe try to transmit the info between steps via an artifact?

title: Unexpected scale change in the contours during accelerated animation
description:
I uncovered this bug while investigating a critical crash with the same model. (To reproduce the crash, follow steps 1-4 of this (step 2 is optional), and swap "Equivalent Stress" for "Equivalent Total Strain" in step 5.)

DESCRIPTION:

During an accelerated animation, the animation will take some time to be "created" or "prepared." During this time, the unit scale will be accurate. However, the unit scale sometimes changes afterward and will continue to have the wrong scale until the animation is stopped, where the scale will change, but not to the scale it was at previously.

So far, I have only gotten the bug to occur with the attached model with the below steps. The scale changed from [1.4e-10 to 1.267] to [0 to 8735.8], which suspiciously is the conversion factor between psi and Pa. Note that even when I run the animation in metric mode, the scale will still multiply by the same factor. 1.4e-10 and 1.267 are the minimum and maximum bounds of the psi values in all frames of the animation.

(SOLVED: When stopping the animation, the scale will decrease by a factor of ~10000, but there is some nuance. The maximum value in the scale does not decrease by exactly that factor, but something close to it; and the minimum value increases from 0 to some small value. I found that the reason why this happens is when upon stopping the animation, the scale changes to the bounds of the last frame of the animation. It is a coincidence that this scaling happens to be within 0.05% of a 10000x scaling factor from before.)

TO REPRODUCE:
  1. Open the attached model.
  2. Go to "Expansion Settings" in the tree. Click on the one of the leftmost checkboxes to enable "expand all results." This is necessary to get the required data that the animation will iterate over.
  3. Change the units to the bottom-most one, which is U.S. Customary. This is necessary to be able to solve the model.
  4. Solve the model.
  5. Go to "Equivalent Stress" in the tree.
  6. Go to the animation graph window.
  7. Set the frames to result sets by clicking the blue button directly to the left of the frame text box in the animation toolbar (this does not affect the bug, but it makes the bug easier to see).
  8. Run an animation, making sure accelerated animation is enabled. Notice how the for the first ~4 seconds of the graph, the animation is being "created" or "prepared" and the units are correct. Then, suddenly the scale change will happen and the model will be dark blue.

PICTURES:

Unit scale when the animation is stopped or not playing:


(The correct) Unit scale while the animation is being "created"/"prepared":


(The incorrect) unit scale after the animation has been "created"/"prepared":



It has been discovered that this bug does not appear in 242.

  • Start fluent with GPU solver
  • Read cas/dat
  • Execute cpu-gpu-numerics.jou (May not be strictly necessary, but this accounts for other known CPU-GPU numerics differences.)
  • Run one iteration
  • Notice large restart bounce, even in flow equations
By dumping the rule output from the GPU solver, it seems that the turbulence viscosity is being initialized from the initial conditions rather than being read in from the dat file.

Tentatively assigning to reacting flow team since it seems to occur only with mixtures. If time permits I can also try to investigate during hardening.

title: Friction state mapping between Mechanical and STD motion
description:
The current mapping rule to display friction states is as follows

                  STD post -------> Mechanical
value = 0(non contact) -----> 0 (near)
value = 1(Stiction)  ---------> 3 (Sticking)
value = 2(Static)  -----------> 3 (Sticking)
value = 3(Transient) --------> 3 (Sticking)
value = 4(Dynamic) --------> 2 (Sliding)


In this case, Static & Transient states are treated as the "Sticking" state in Mechanical.
It is quite weird because a contour result of a spinning disk under the dynamic threshold velocity indicates that it is under "Sticking" state even though it is sliding.


I guess that the mapping should be changed as follows.
         STD post --------------> Mechanical
value = 0(non contact) -----> 0 (near)
value = 1(Stiction)  ---------> 3 (Sticking)
value = 2(Static)  -----------> 2 (Sliding)
value = 3(Transient) --------> 2 (Sliding)
value = 4(Dynamic) --------> 2 (Sliding)


================ (Manual part)=========================

        < Mechanical Rule >


              
           < Standalone Post Rule >

"

Thankfully, I still have a 2024 version of MotorCAD installed, and it runs transient thermal envelopes just fine, so I am still "operational". But I am concerned about this.  

 

This program malfunction needs to be fixed because thermal envelopes are extremely important to my work --------- and are an especially vital "deliverable" to most customers, who like to use them to estimate how they can safely load our motors in their products ("peak" loads).

 

I was attempting to run S2 thermal envelopes using the "simple transient" settings in the THERMAL module. I have yet to try "custom duty cycle" settings, but I would be surprised if that made any difference, since it seems like the program "break" causes failure of any transient configurations at all. title: Two .csv file are exported using "Export Transient / Harmonic Force" in Maxwell
description:
I was working on a PyAEDT example to export harmonic force. In Maxwell GUI the feature on which is wrapped the PyAEDT method to export the element based harmonic force is “Export Transient / Harmonic Force”.


In 3D magnetic transient, after enabling element based volumetric harmonic force and solving the model, it is possible to “Export Transient / Harmonic Force”. But the export generates two .csv files:

  • One called “index.csv” which for some cases it looks like contains equivalent circuit parameters, or in some cases basically it is an empty file. This file is created in the working directory by default if no file path is specified.
  • The other called “Maxwellharforce.csv” which contains the desired volumetric harmonic forces. This file is created in a subfolder named as the analysis setup from which is exported the forces after solving the model in the working directory by default.

This is confusing because the user does not know which file is the correct one. The Maxwell documentation does not help because it only says the forces are exported in a .csv format. Also, I do not understand why “index.csv” is created and what should be the content of such file?

Instead, if I proceed to export the forces through the field calculator, after enabling element based volumetric harmonic force and solving the model, I get a .fld file with listed elements with empty forces. In 3D magnetic transient, this procedure works well in case we want to export element-based surface harmonic forces. Below two slides illustrate how to export harmonic forces in a .fld file:



Attached you will find an .aedt project containing two designs, one created from script with PyAEDT (“pyaedt_example”) and the other one is from my colleague Tiziana Bertoncelli. In both models I tested “Export Transient / Harmonic Force”.

title: Endurance limit for sine sweep loading in the Mechanical Fatigue Tool
description:
The Mechanical Fatigue Tool (FT) uses different endurance limits for single frequency loading and sine sweep loading. 

 

For the single frequency calculation, the FT uses the last data point on the SN curve to establish the endurance limit (e.g.,1e8 cycles at 30 MPa).

 

 

For alternating stresses below 30 MPa, life in seconds is reported as 1e8 cycles divided by the frequency (e.g. for a frequency of 375 Hz, life = 1e8 cycles/375 Hz = 2.67e5 seconds).

 

For the sine sweep calculation, FT sets the endurance limit to be 1e32 cycles at the lowest stress on the SN curve (e.g., 30 MPa).  So, for alternating stresses below 30 MPa, life is reported as 1e32 cycles divided by the frequency (e.g., life = 1e32 cycles/375 Hz = 2.67e39 seconds). This large maximum life creates a skewed contour plot.

 

The behavior of the FT should be consistent for single frequency loading a sine sweep loading, so the FT should be modified to use the last data point on the SN curve to establish the endurance limit for sine sweep loading.

title: Bearing Property window in Motion Pre: Axial vs. Radial Direction Inconsistency (Visual)
description:
The bearing graphic suggests that the X direction (blue arrow) represents the axial direction. However, the stiffness matrix indicates that the Z direction corresponds to the axial bearing direction.

This is confirmed by applying a deformation of 0.05 mm in the Z direction, where FxDx and FyDy values are equal—consistent with axial behavior. Conversely, applying deformation in the X direction results in unequal translational stiffness values, which contradicts the expected symmetry for axial deformation.


Example:

A deformation of 0.03 mm in X yields non-zero stiffness values.
A deformation of 0.03 mm in Z yields the expected zero values.



Conclusion:

This suggests that the Z axis is the actual axial direction, despite the graphic indicating otherwise. A revision is recommended to ensure that the bearing axes and their corresponding colors are consistent with the global coordinate system.

title: pyDFPSound - Compute third octave levels operator always returns zero value at last band 16000Hz
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
pyDFPSound: Compute third octave levels operator always returns zero value at last band 16000Hz

Data:
Python files, WAV signal.

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
DPF operator: "compute_one_third_octave_levels_from_psd"
Use the attached python script and the attached WAV signal.
The python script will load the "White_noise_mono.wav"and compute PSD levels in Pa^2/HZ.
    >note that path to sound dpf dll and wav file will need to be updated for local use.
The output of this PSD computation is used as input for third octave level computation.
It will print the Third Octave frequencies and dB levels.
The last band for Third octave always returns a zero value irrespective of signal used --> BUG



Expected behavior:
dB value of last band somewhat comparable to what returned from SAS.

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
An index issue would cause the last 1/3-octave band to be empty (the loop would stop after the previous iteration).
Solution:
Mostly, an additional iteration is done.
Also algo's indexing was changed slightly (1-based -> 0-based) for better clarity, and the last band's upper limit was added in constants, as it's needed to know where to stop summing squared amplitudes.

title: Dataset error for imported layout comps with dataset dependent materials
description:
This bug is related to "1129095: Variable error when plotting fields on a layout component." Assume a layout component has a material which is dependent on its project dataset (e.g. $dsTest). When we import this material and try to solve it, two errors are observed:
  1. If no $dsTest dataset exists in the parent design, then the material is not able to be read properly giving out an error.
  2. If $dsTest exists in the parent design, then the parent design dataset is read instead of layout component dataset, which is wrong.
Thus two issues are:
  1. Incorrect mapping of layout dataset name to something unique (may be compName_datasetName). Solving this will solve issue no. 2 discussed above.
  2. Incorrect writing of dataset to the solver file. Solving this will solve issue no. 1 discussed above.
I have attached a test model here, but all other steps need to be copied from the related bug D1129095.

This issue has always existed, and should be considered a new development. This is not a regression.

There are only two components in the model: (1) a flat PCB component; (2) a MCAD component. However, when combining these two components in the same design gives the following mesh error: 

"Initial Surface mesh generation failed. Automatic fallback is not supported for surface meshes. Please switch to alternative meshes manually."



The customer has tried different initial mesh settings and this errors persists in all cases. title: warning messages from Genequiv logfile should be pushed to message manager in AEDT for the new Q3D/Maxwell RLGC dynamic link component
description:
Hi,

The RLGC fitting tool does few things behind the scenes. For example, if the received training data for "RL" does not form a causal pair when the impedance data is being put together then we look at the fitting error achieved if it exceeds a prescribed threshold (5%) then we correct for the causality of the data yet do another fit to the causally corrected data, compare the original fit against the fit to the causally corrected data pick the better of the two. We also write a (warning) message in the Genequiv logfile. Yet as another example, we check the fit to "R" and if it is worse than 1% (relative) error and the target fitting error chosen exceeds 1e-4 then we decrease it to 1e-5 try another fit with the hopes of improving the fit to "R". Again, we do write a (warning) message in the Genequiv logfile. The objective here is to postprocess Genequiv logfile for these messages and then push them into the AEDT message manager. Here is a sample logfile:

genequiv:progress 0:
genequiv:message Reading input data:
genequiv:progress 5:
genequiv:message starting:
genequiv:progress 95:
genequiv:message ending:
genequiv:warning 113 R fitting error exceeded 1%. Reducing error tolerance to 1.0e-5 to achieve a better fit.
genequiv:progress 5:
genequiv:message starting:
genequiv:progress 95:
genequiv:message ending:
We'd like that message to be pushed as a status message into the AEDT message manager during the circuit dynamic link simulation with the Q3D\Maxwell RLGC component. 

@Ryan Schimizzi @Matthew Young

title: bidl.exe 'include' statement uses only current folder to solve path
description:
The bidl.exe binary uses only the current folder to look for the included files. The issue has been spotted with AnsImage2.idl in the interfaces folder which includes AnsysCommon.idl. When compiled using the VS projects in the interfaces folder, it works. When build from another folder, it fails. 

Expected actions:
-> bidl.exe binary uses the same folder to solve the "include" as it uses to solve the idl "import"
-> When inclusion fails, make bidl.exe fail with an explicit error. Current, the not found inclusion is just ignored which leads to misbehavior later - not necessarily easy to spot if you ignore the initial problem.

title: HFSS Solver: It didn't process spice model of component correctly.
description:
There is a cap component with spice model in attached design. if I put the spice of model into CAP component, the result will not make sense, it seems VDD and vss are shorted. But if delete the spice model, result will be correct.

20250613 Update: This error is likely caused by a mismatch between Spice nodes and layout pins. This was done for expediency, but we can't do this long-term, since the build machine and developer machines must build the same configs to have any hope of debugging problems in the future.

We need to reconcile any changes that needed to be made in the Release-BuildMachine config and capture them in all configs that developers build.

title: Fluent Pro License Command Execution Inconsistency with Documentation
description:
One of Ansys Korea's channel partner, TSNE, identified an inconsistency regarding Pro license usage via command-line execution.

According to 2025R2 documentation, Pro license should be executable via command-line. However, when attempting to run it on Windows cmd, an error message states that Pro license cannot be launched in command mode.



Upon reviewing previous bug reports, it seems this may have been intended behavior. However, I discovered an additional point: when a specific environment variable (FLUENT_STARTED_FROM_LAUNCHER) is set, command-line execution with Pro license works successfully. I've tested this and confirmed that it runs as expected.

I would like to clarify the following:
  • Is it acceptable to share the environment variable workaround with TSNE?
  • Or should we treat the documentation as incorrect and report it as such?
I would appreciate your guidance on how to proceed.

Thank you!

title: Matrix reordering file for volumetric shell elements
description:
This defect is spawned from DE1320438. In attached project, user sets volumetric shell elements

With this setting, we will have 4 instead of 2 matrix bandwidths because this condition is frequency dependent. For instance
adapt frequency 5GHz (no tree-cotree, volumetric shell elements not triggered) bandwidth 19.7
10MHz (no tree-cotree, volumetric shell elements triggered) bandwidth 20.5
5.05MHz (tree-cotree, volumetric shell elements triggered) bandwidth 24.7
Note that matrix dimension remains the same when volumetric shell elements are triggered. So matrix solver will not reject the file but will lead to incorrect result or crash as matrix is different.

Therefore when saving matrix reordering file, we need to record this info the same way as tree-cotree. Please also take care mesh fusion solver as well.

title: Mesh plot cutoff at envelope if design has postprocessing variable
description:
See attached design with two components. One is set to do mesh assembly and has priority level enabled. The higher priority's envelope will cut out lower priority component and have it meshed with the higher priority component. This is expected. 

However, if design has any post processing variable, the mesh plot of the lower priority component will stop at the boundary of the mesh envelope. 


Step to reproduce:
  1. Open attached design, make sure priority level is enabled and comp_lumped_port set to do mesh assembly and has higher priority.
  2. Generate mesh.
  3. Plot mesh on the lower priority component (metal_block).
  4. Observe that, if there is no post-processing variable defined, the mesh plot will include the part that's within the envelope but not intersecting higher priority component.
  5. Delete the mesh plot.
  6. Create a post-processing variable.
  7. Plot mesh on the lower priority component again, mesh plot will incorrectly stop at envelope boundary.

AdaptRadius(ref radius, startpoints, endpoints, relativeRadii, wx/n, wy/n, wz/n, boxBodySmall);

title: AIT191: "inf" for anisotropic conductivity in via group causes Prism solver failure
description:
For via groups, with solve-inside set, we derive an anisotropic conductivity on-the-fly.

 

For one of the Seattle cases, somehow the “Conductivity Area Ratio” is getting set to “inf” for a few of the via groups.  This is resulting in an invalid material definition and the solver is failing with an obscure “process gem3d: Invalid matrix entry on tet ID = 6619655” message.

 

In any event, can a change be made such that we always use a finite conductivity?  If it’s “inf”, we can revert to PEC conductivity of 1e+30.

 

Btw, my best guess is “Conductive Area Ratio” is somehow getting a divide by zero, which really shouldn’t happen (unless, perhaps, the area calculation fails?)… just the same, we should be catching the 0 and inf cases.  We don’t have the original Seattle geometry, so figuring out how we got into this state seems unlikely, but hopefully fixing downstream is easy enough.

Case 1. No FEA method:
Average torque (VW) = -90Nm
Balanced flux linkages:

Case 2. Full FEA method (single slot):

FEA plot

Average torque (VW) = -90.14Nm, comparable to caases 1 & 2

Note the negative d-axis inductance:

For reference, Maxwell results are shown below (all conductors are modelled as Solid, with Eddy effects enabled):
Torque = -88Nm -> OK
Flux linkages are balanced as expected and show amplitudes close to flux linkages amplitudes from cases 2.

title: SAS - "Display" images in psycho grid table not created when open file dialog is in use
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
SAS sometimes displays a warning dialog stating that it could not find an image in PNG/ folder. (name of the image may change)
However, the image is in the PNG folder besides the exe.

2 cases are described bellow.
Note that other cases may exist but are still not found. In that case, please create a new bug, with the name of the image not found, a screenshot of the dialog, and a screenshot of the whole state of SAS

Data:
No data

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
Open SAS

Case 1
Open temporal file
Open psycho module
Launch many computation (ex all indicators on several signals). The computation must be long enough to allow doing something else
Set focus back on temporal file
Click on Open file. WAIT long enough before selecting a file and opening it, so that some new indicators which display curves should be filled in psycho table.
Select a file to open, open.
Following dialog opens


Some "display" icons are missing in psycho results grid (empty cell, but clickable anyway)



Case2:
Open a signal, at least 20seconds duration
Set some gain with the volume button, so that the play will clip after 5-10 seconds
Play
BEFORE IT BEGINS TO CLIP: Click on Open file in toolbar. WAIT long enough before selecting a file and opening it, so that some new indicators which display curves should be filled in psycho table.
Select a file to open, open.
Same kind of dialog opens, with PNG/Volume_clipped_48x48.png cited as not found

Expected behavior:
No dialog, no error

Dev notes: possible solutions:
Option 1: use PNGs in ressources -> OK for our code, KO for code generated from wxFormBuilder

Optoin 2: change directory before / restore after creating images in very specific places (call on timer): OK, but difficult to identify all places where this may happen. actually identified: 
    • wxBitmap creation in gui_BatchComputationResults::OnActualizeGrid
    • Images in GKnob (to be precised), probably at least the clipped version (see GKnob::UseClippedKnob)
    • Others ? -> look for wxTimer objects
Option 3: Create wxImage as class attribute, initialized during ctor

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
During the display of the wxFileDialog, the currentWorkingDirectory is probably modified, leading to the relative path PNG/XXX to no longer work.

Solution:
Create images at a time when no "Open" dialog may be displayed: during the creation of the containing class.

Impacts:

title: IM Lab vs. E-Mag discrepancy with FEA Advanced + FEA Map Resistance
description:
I have to report some unexpected results for the IM. This is originally from a customer ticket.

The case is related to the E-mag vs. Lab comparison for a MTPA operating point. The Lab performance are computed using the Advanced FEA method with the FEA Map option for the rotor resistance.

For the considered machine, the MTPA point at 8400 rpm and 395 A (max current) is analysed. Lab gives the following results:
  • rotor frequency is 16.5 Hz.
  • rotor cage loss is 7200 W.
  • torque is 205.7 N m
The MTPA operating point at 395 A is searched also with E-mag approach (sensitivity analysis varying the slip with SLP FEA) and the following results are derived:
  • rotor frequency is 19.25 Hz.
  • rotor cage loss is 8720 W.
  • torque is 208.3 N m.
The torque value is good, is it seems that the cage resistance in the two models is different: lower rotor frequency and cage loss in Lab, meaning that the resistance is under estimated.

I have checked using the analytical resistance with the FEA Advanced Lab, and in the same MTPA operating point, I get this:
  • rotor frequency is 20.5 Hz.
  • cage loss is 8920 W.
  • torque is 205.7 N m.
The rotor frequency and cage loss estimation is now much closer to E-Mag. 

To conclude the comparison, I compared the referred rotor resistance from the two Lab methods (analytical and FEA)  with the FEA Map resistance lookup table and I got this for the analytical lab approach:



It looks that the resistance used by Lab within the equivalent circuit with the analytical resistance model is very close to the values from the FEA Map LUT. Since the analytical resistance methods gives good results, this confirms that the FEA Map resistance LUT have reasonable values which should produce a good match against E-Mag FEA.

However, if I now compare the referred resistance used by lab eq. circ. when the resistance FEA Map is enable, they look quite different than the original LUT:



The resistance used in the equivalent circuit is quite below the LUT values (leading to lower losses and rotor frequency).

I think the original LUT from the FEA Map method is correct, but somewhere in the code (maybe in the interpolation or parameter transformation) the information is changed to a wrong value.

I know it's a bit long comment, but I am fully available to go through this with you and help finding the issue within the code.

Let me know!

I tag @Francesco Papini into this, since he's the direct Magna contact.

title: GUI Mismatch in Antipad Handling and DC Shorted Error Behavior in SIwave
description:
Starting from version 2022, the CAD input process ensures a default clearance between vias and cutouts by recognizing the presence of antipads defined around the vias. This is a change from earlier versions (2021 and below), where the Validation Check would ignore antipads if a cutout was present, potentially resulting in a DC shorted error.

To align the Validation Check with the solver setup behavior, this has been revised. Consequently, even in versions 2022 and above, if the antipad is removed from the padstack, a DC shorted error will still occur.

However, this updated behavior does not immediately reflect in the GUI, and it takes effect only when the Padstack window is turned on and off once.

title: Missing electric potential boundary condition on an FS interface and difference in temperature results for a CHT case with Joule heating

The attached model consists of a solid pipe (from VM-Thermal-006) enclosed by a fluid domain.

The fluid and thermal boundary conditions were set-up in Discovery and the corresponding rh file is modified via an Apollo test script to include electric potential conditions.

In the existing Apollo implementation of Joule heating, it is assumed that the FS interface is a part of the Apollo entry named "Bonded Contact". In this case, no additional electric potential boundary conditions are required to be specified at the FS interface. A preview of FS interface as a part of bonded contact entry is shown below:


However, when we export an rh file from disco, we get different Apollo entries for bonded contacts and FS interface as shown below. 

In this case, we get an error if we do not specify electric potential boundary conditions at the FS interface.


Furthermore, for the attached model, the temperature results are very different compared to Fluent and Artemis data



PS: The attached rh file has the electric potential boundary conditions setup in the model

title: SAS - Wrong value in the highest band when computing octave-band levels with a frequency weighting (A, B, C)
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
The last octave band (16000 Hz) is wrong if computed with a frequency weighting.
The issue does not occur with other bands, or if no weighting is used (ie when using SPL).

Data:

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
Open the attached signal
Compute its spectrum
Switch to 1/3 Octave
Apply weighting A
Pick up the levels of the 2 highest bands (12500 & 16000 Hz)
>> 38.82 dBA & 27.46 dBA
Switch to Octave
Pick up the level of the highest band (16000 Hz)
>> 27.46 dBA

Expected behavior:
If you repeat this without the A-weighting, you get a value that is larger than both the last 2 1/3 octave bands, which is what you would expect
So here, the value should be larger than 38.82 dBA. 39.13 dBA to be precise

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
The last band is assigned the last 1/3-octave band value, instead of summing the last 2 bands
A similar fix was done for non-weighted computation, but weighted case was omitted

Solution:
Replicate the same fix for the 3 weighted cases (that is, sum the last 2 1/3-octave bands)

title: [LPE] Raytracing GPU crash when node visibility is set to false during simulation
description:
DESCRIPTION:
Data:
Based on the test "ReflectionTests.WithRaytracedReflection"

Notes:
  • When no point light is in the scene, there is a crash

Steps to reproduce:
  • Run the test "ReflectionTests.WithRaytracedReflection" by replacing with this code 
[Theory]
[MemberData(nameof(EnvData))]
public void WithRaytracedReflection(string envName, string envRootPath)
{
    _simulationParameters.BetaFeatures.RaytracedReflection = true;

    var outputType = ImageOutputType.XYZOutput;
    var scene      = LoadTestScene(envRootPath);
    var scene = LoadTestScene(envRootPath);

    var (tester, simulation) = CreateSimulationTester(scene,
                                                        _simulationDebugParameters,
                                                        2048,
                                                        1024);

    // Bug 1322721: [LPE] Raytracing specular does not work properly
    // If no point light is present in the scene, the test crashes
    var lighting = scene.FindNodesContainingName("Lighting01");
    foreach (var sceneNode in lighting)
    {
        sceneNode.IsVisible = false;
    }

    var camera01 = scene.ExtractCamera("01");
    camera01.Adaptation = 36792.89f;
    var poseCamera01 = camera01.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky_{envName}", outputType);

    var camera02 = scene.ExtractCamera("02");
    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera02.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky_{envName}", outputType);

    var camera03 = scene.ExtractCamera("03");
    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera03.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky_{envName}", outputType);

    var camera04 = scene.ExtractCamera("04");
    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera04.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"AtmosphericSky_{envName}", outputType);

    tester.CompareResults(PixelTolerance, ImageTolerance);
    var textureId = simulation.CreateTexture(Path.Combine(FileUtils.RootDataDirectory, "Input/Resources/Textures/HDR_forest.hdr"), ColorSpace.Automatic).objectId;
    simulation.ActivateImageBasedSky(textureId, 10000, 0);
    var direction = new Vector3D(0.1, 1.0, 0.1);
    direction.Normalize();
    simulation.SetDirectionalLightVisibility(true);
    simulation.SetDirectionalLightDirection(direction.X, direction.Y, direction.Z);
    simulation.SetDirectionalLightExitance(10000.0);
    simulation.EnableDirectionalShadows(true);

    camera01.Parent.Pose = poseCamera01;
    tester.Execute($"HdriSky_{envName}", outputType);

    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera02.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"HdriSky_{envName}", outputType);

    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera03.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"HdriSky_{envName}", outputType);

    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera04.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"HdriSky_{envName}", outputType);

    simulation.DisableSky();
    simulation.SetDirectionalLightVisibility(false);
    camera01.Adaptation = 10.89f;
    foreach (var sceneNode in lighting)
    {
        sceneNode.IsVisible = true;
    }

    Bug 1322721: [LPE] Raytracing specular does not work properly
    HDRI sky is still rendered into the specular reflections, whereas it should not
    camera01.Parent.Pose = poseCamera01;
    tester.Execute($"Night_{envName}", outputType);

    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera02.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"Night_{envName}", outputType);

    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera03.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"Night_{envName}", outputType);

    camera01.Parent.Pose = camera04.Parent.Pose;
    tester.Execute($"Night_{envName}", outputType);

    tester.CompareResults(PixelTolerance, ImageTolerance);

}
Expected behavior:
  • HDRI must be not visible into the specular reflections
  • User texture coordinates channel must be picked according the user's provided ones
  • Texture of the ground plane must be visible (anisotropic sampler?)
  • MultiPoint lights must contribute into specular reflection
  • When no point light is in the scene, the simulation must run
Reproducible (always, never, often, sometimes): 
always

Machine configuration:
Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version):
  • OS : N/A
  • GPU : N/A
  • Driver GPU : N/A
  • Hardware specific :  N/A

==============================================

CLOSING SUMMARY:

Cause (if regression set an VRXP_REGRESSION tag):

Instead of setting PhysicalPointLight node object visibility to false the test was hiding a group containing multiple nodes.
The real cause was that sfs have their geometry in acceleration structure and index/vertex buffers.
When we set visibility to false the geometry is removed but the top acceleration structure don't have the geometries indexes updated accordingly. A crash was occuring in raytrace helpers function when fetching the bindless buffers based on the index offset and the index of the instance hit by the ray.

Solution:

When a modelInstance is added or removed the top acceleration structure is now rebuilt.

Impacts (if there is a risk set an AVX_RISK_HIGH, AVX_RISK_MEDIUM or AVX_RISK_LOW tag):

Notes:

A second crash was occurring when running the test, this time linked to the validation layers. "GPU Assisted Validation". By default the layer setting "Generate warning on out of bounds accesses even if buffer robustness is enabled" is set to true. In SDK version (1.4.304 and maybe more) this feature has a bug that hardly slow the program and can lead to a crash.
The feature has been removed in latest SDK version: 1.4.321 and the issue is now fixed.

    Turned on HFSS Mesh Fusion (With Dynamic Surface Resolution on)
    Removed unused definitions from the Tools > Project Tools menu

title: Q3D Prime Mesh Made Finer for Length Based Mesh Operation Than Requested
description:
Using Q3D with the Prime mesher on a Samtec model of a 20x20 array of 0.9mm square pins with 0.1mm gaps, a 6mm mesh operation was added in design 5_, which was meant to improve the DCRL mesh from the left to the right images below.  The concern after seeing the mesh in the image on the left was the DCRL solver accuracy with such high aspect ratio elements.  Later I found that the DCRL result appears insensitive to DCRL mesh quality with answers appearing by eye to be well within 1%.  



However, the 6mm length mesh operation is very important for the ACRL solve efficiency.  The 6mm mesh operation reduced the ACRL mesh from the left image below to right image (so more dense seeding for ACRL than DCRL).  The original ACRL RMS mesh length ~ 3mm, yielded good answers and a fast solve time.  After the 6mm mesh length operation was added, the ACRL RMS mesh length reduced to <1.3mm.  The ACRL solve time approximately went up 3x from 11 minutes to 31 minutes as a result of something I didn't ask to be done.  Why does the ACRL mesher take a 6mm mesh operation and reduce the ACRL RMS edge length from ~3mm to <1.3mm? 



Look for "WORKS" or "FAILS" in design names as well as other description in the design name.

2025.1 Project


2025.2 Project

A March 7, 2025R2 build was used for the results above.

Ravi suggested this be assigned to Werner.

title: [SSH Remote] Empty file created on download, handle not removed until optiSLang closed
description:
See BugBash line 45

"If the download fails, sometimes a file with the name of the 'to be downloaded file' is created with 0 KB size that cannot be deleted until the optiSLang instance is closed!"

Solution:
The root cause is that libmssh creates the empty file but does not remove it on error. The fix needs to be implemented in libmssh.
Additionally, the version needs to be increased and the package needs to be rebuilt and consumed in optiSLang.

title: [SSH Remote] Input file from slot via files tab doesn't work
description:
See BugBash feedback line 46

1. define an input file in the files tab as absolute path
2. Select use path from slot
3. The uploaded file is always the same from the absolute path definition

Solution:

We need to implement a custom PLM for the Files tab for Remote Profiles or at least SSH Remote Profile.
The current implementation is too specific and not in line with how optiSLang behaves, e.g. you currently don't need to specify specifically that a file should be sent or received. We should decouple this whole Files tab functionality from the Operator part of the Remote Profile functionality and instead integrate it directly into the Files Tab. This would also allow any node (that supports the Files tab) to send/receive files using a Remote Profile.

title: Not all conductive mask layers have correct material after import
description:
In 25.2, if "Import Shield Layers" is selected for brd import then these layers will be defined as conductors and have the material defined in the source design including nonzero conductivity if present.  However, other mask layers with conductive materials are still converted to dielectric.  In addition, without enabling "Import Shield Layers" even the EMI_SHIELD_* layers will be converted to dielectric with conductivity removed.  Customers expect that material properties set in the source design will be honored and conductor/dielectric type be chosen appropriately based on conductivity, even if they are not importing the shield layer geometry.

To reproduce:
  1. Import attached design either with "Import Shield Layers" turned off or with it turned on with custom layer names EMI_SHIELD_S_BOTTOM for the bottom shield and EMI_SHIELD_S_TOP for the top shield.
  2. Note in the Messages window warnings from anstranslator about materials with non-zero conductivity and the associated layers being converted to dielectric:
    1. With "Import Shield Layers" off this will apply to both EMI_SHIELD_S_* and SEL_PLT_*
    2. With "Import Shield Layers" on as described above this will apply only to SEL_PLT_*

  • Also copy <UserGivenLinux64Dir>../licensingclient/language folder to the same resources/Solver/licensingclient-- this is for proper messaging when the FMU is run in Linux command line tools.

title: Need to mark Fluid specific result variables invalid when scoped to solid side of fluid solid interface with per face results option

1. Enable the beta option 'Results on individual faces' and restart discovery

title: Share topology for tank-like geometries results in bad mesh if dynamic tolerances are not used
description:
Consider the following geometry, a hollow tank with thick walls split in two:


Using share topology with the default settings such that the interface between the two halves is shared results in a bad mesh. With multizone meshing, the mesher stalls until it fails with the error message:


With tetrahedral meshing, the outer edge of one of the halves attempts to connect with the inner edge of the other half, resulting in an unphysical mesh:


The workaround I found was to, when performing the share topology operation, enable the "Force Share" option, reducing the "Not-shared face pairs" number to zero:


The mesh is then created correctly - for example, with multizone meshing:


Perhaps this isn't really a bug, but is more of a potential pain point for users that should be documented/recommended.

See attached file for example geometry where the topology share is not performed correctly.

Found in TD 26R1 build 2025-06-11.

Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version):
  • OS: N/A
  • GPU: N/A
  • Driver GPU: N/A
  • Hardware specific: N/A

==============================================

CLOSING SUMMARY:

Cause (if regression set an VRXP_REGRESSION tag):
At first frame, when initiating the for pass, the diffuse sky map is not yet rendered so the fog binding is set to a black texture.
So if we do not have any sky or fog update during simulation (same if the fog parameter transmitted are the same) the fog rendering will be only black.

Solution:
Ensure that the fog pass binding are correctly updated when the sky has been updated or computed.

title: Licenses not incrementing/decrementing as expected with Ansys Shared Web Licensing

When I start multiple instances of STK using Ansys Shared Web Licensing UAT and view the client licensing app, the licenses for Enterprise, Premium-Air, Premium-Space, Pro, and ODTK do not decrement as expected. I have attached a spreadsheet which shows this progression. I start out with 4 licenses entitlements each for Enterprise, Premium-Air, Premium-Space, Pro, and ODTK, with each test scenario specifying what type of STK was started, how many licenses are used/available for each license type, and the PIDs assigned to each license type as an application is started.

In the test, I start out with STK Enterprise and see the PID assigned to Enterprise in the client licensing app and the used/available number updating as expected. However, as I create more instances of STK (Premium-Air, Premium-Space, Pro), I see a PID that was once assigned to Enterprise now also being assigned to Air when I start Premium-Air, for example, which is not expected behavior.

See the attached model.  The static structural system has 3 substeps to ramp up to the full load, and I store results at all time points.


Looking at the Equivalent Stress result under the static analysis, you can see the maximum overall stress ramp up from ~14kpsi to ~150kpsi.  After running the Harmonic analysis, I create the Fatigue Diagram object and you can tell from the steady stresses in the plot that it is pulling from the first substep (14kpsi):


When I pull the drop down it shows 3 steps available but if I click on any step, it always resets back to 1 and will always use the first substep:

title: Forces in Eddy current solver
description:
Dear Team,

I have a case where the customer says that the help document was unclear on forces in the eddy current solver.

  • The force experienced by a body in which there are induced eddy currents is the instantaneous force; the AC and DC forces are just a decomposition of that into a constant part (the time average) and an oscillating part (the full signal minus the time average). However, if the period of the oscillation is much shorter than the structural response time of the structure, then the structure will effectively feel the DC force, whereas if the period of the oscillation is similar to or longer than the structural response time of the structure, then the structure will effectively feel the instantaneous force.
  • The instantaneous force and hence the AC force oscillate at twice the frequency of the input signal (that bit is clear in the documentation), but they are not necessarily in-phase with the input signal (that bit was not clear). If there is a phase shift, it is due to the impedance (inductance and/or capacitance) of the body. This also causes the instantaneous force to get offset vertically, leading to a non-zero DC force. This point caused particular confusion, because the oscillations were always about zero, hence a time average would always be zero.
  • The phase shift above is between the induced EMF (in-phase with the input signal) and the induced current (phase shifted). This can be anywhere between + 90 degrees (purely inductive) and -90 degrees (purely capacitive). The corresponding vertical shift in the instantaneous force is such that the DC force can be anywhere between +/- the amplitude of the AC force.

These are the points that were not clear in the documentation. Can we add more information to make the document clear?

title: Incorrect voltage result value on user-specified current density BC location
description:
Found in Artemis regression test, SingleBodyJouleHeating.

In the Artemis Cromwell database, the sign of user-specified current BC value on the bottomWall is opposite to the sign of the same BC value taken from the pcas database exported from Fluent GPU:
Artemis database entry
electrostatic/boundary-condition/20/minus/current = [string] scalar(value = 100000, variable = current)

Fluent GPU/Pcas export database entry
electrostatic/boundary-condition/20/minus/current = [string] scalar(value = -100000, variable = current)
The case file exported from Artemis was read into Fluent GPU, then the pcas file was written using this command: (%gpuapp-write-partitioned-case "single_body_joule_heating" 0).
The opposite sign of the current BC value results in incorrect voltages reported on the bottomWall location (wall_zone_2 in Fluent) - e.g., Artemis reports max of 4.9 V while Fluent reports a max of 5.09 V. The user-specified voltage on the topWall location (wall_zone_1 in Fluent) is 5 V. Note the current value is displayed as positive in Fluent even though it's negative in the exported pcas database.


Please see the two Cromwell database.txt files attached - one generated by Artemis and the other generated in the Fluent GPU pcas export. Perhaps we need some of the entries in the Fluent/pcas database that are missing from the Artemis one?
  • electrostatic/initial-voltage/53 = [string] scalar(value = 0, variable = voltage)
  • electrostatic/boundary-condition/20/minus/contact-resistance = [string] scalar(value = 0, variable = contact-resistance)
  • electrostatic/boundary-condition/20/minus/contact-resistance-on = [bool] false

title: TAU Mesh Ignores Surface Approximation Normal Deviation Mesh Operation for Angle > 30deg
description:
The below/attached test project was created to test the TAU and Classic mesher regarding mesh operation defeaturing.  This submission is focused on the Surface Approximation mesh operation.



The surface approximation mesh operation Normal Deviation is applied to each of Box2/Circle2, Box3/Circle3, Box4/Circle4, and Box5/Circle5 with values of 30deg, 45deg, 60deg, and 90deg respectively.  For example, here is for the 30deg setting for Box2/Circle2.


The classic mesher creates expected faceting for the 2D circles and for the filleted edges.  See design 1_ClassicNormalDeviation.



For the filleted edges, 45deg and 60deg settings both yield 45deg arc resolution (2 edges around the 90deg bend) because a 90deg angle can only be broken evenly into 22.5deg, 30deg, 45deg, and 90deg increments.  However, Circle4 is able to be segmented as a hexagon.  The 90deg setting yields a single segment chamfered edge as expected for Box5 and a square for Circle5.  Significantly, the tetrahedra count drops from 680 for the default to 371, 344, and 104 tetrahedra for the 45deg, 60deg, and 90deg cases.  

In contrast, the TAU mesher does not respect the surface approximation normal deviation setting greater than 30deg.  See design 2_TAUNormalDeviation. As shown in red, boxes 3, 4, and 5 have 30deg arc resolution (3 edges around the radiused bends), and the 2D circles use 12 facets (30deg resolution).



Comparing the defeaturing of Classic vs TAU up close, the 90deg and 45deg Classic cases provide a substantial mesh reduction, but also good aspect ratios on the filleted edges.  TAU has a poor aspect ratios on the filleted edges and does not reduce the mesh.

A further study in designs:
3_Classic90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation
4_TAU90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation
uses the manual settings combination that I have used for many years as my "go-to", which is to enable both normal deviation with a big arc resolution value (45deg or 90deg) and max surface deviation that ultimately controls the angular resolution.  This combination allows defeaturing electrically small radii while preserving larger rounds within mechanical tolerances.


For this study, I set normal deviation to 90deg for Boxes/Circles 2 through 4, and set surface deviation from 0.01mm to 0.1mm.  

The Classic mesher in 3_Classic90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation (except for an outlier for Box3) demonstrates the ability to combine these mesh operations as expected.  Note the circle objects (the electrically larger objects) demonstrating a facet count smoothly decreasing from 16 to 4 as the maximum deviation increases.


The TAU mesher in design 4_TAU90degNormalDeviationPlusSurfaceDeviation ignores the 90deg normal deviation setting, which makes the maximum surface deviation setting irrelevant/ignored as well.  The initial mesh and final mesh for this design is exactly the same as for 2_TAUNormalDeviation, despite the mesh operation settings being completely different.



The findings are that:
1) the TAU mesher cannot be used to defeature geometry with the surface approximation mesh normal deviation operation higher than 30deg.
2) the aspect ratio of the TAU mesh on the small radiused features is substantially worse than the Classic mesher, which could lead to less accurate/reliable solutions at low signal levels.
3) the Classic mesher can reduce the mesh size of models with electrically small radiused features dramatically compared with the TAU mesher.  The 90deg case for Classic is over 3.5x less mesh than TAU.

Many customer CAD models have electrically small, but long radiused features which severely impact the mesh size, run time, and RAM usage.  The capability to defeature is extremely important, but TAU does not offer defeaturing like Classic.  Unfortunately, Classic often fails and has been reported as increasingly failing in 2025R2.  TAU should either respect the mesh operation setting (this is what should happen given the huge gains), or if the development of that improvement will take more than one release, then a warning message should be issued during the interim, alerting the user that the mesh operation is being implemented as 30deg despite the user setting >30deg.

If TAU can work as expected with the surface approximation mesh operation, the mesh could be reduced >3x on standard CAD features such as electrically small fillets.

title: VCollab Parameter Report Differences
description:
Created one bug to keep track of all current param report issues on VCollab's end. Investigated the others and a lot of them ended up not being bugs. 
  • General - the <file> section has a "title" attribute. The content that appears in this section is correct; however, it should be called "label" instead of "title"
  • scdocx native support - reports do not have the Spaceclaim version included. We would like this to be included if this is possible.
  • General - the <section> format should be used over <table> unless the data is tabular. Taken from our schema:
    • Metadata MUST be stored as <text>/<number>/<boolean>/<date> values in <section>s instead of in <table>s where feasible. Tables SHOULD be reserved for metadata that would make sense to display in a chart.
    • Tables should be used to describes sets of data (such as parameter tables, charts, etc.). They MUST NOT be used to describe key-value-pair data. That should be done using the value elements grouped into sections.
  • CylAbaqusInput.odb - components section is missing information

title: SIMPLORER_HOME and SIWAVE_INSTALL_DIR environment variables are not available right after 25.2 Unified Install
description:
The environment variable SIMPLORER_HOME is created by the installer pointing to the installation directory. Until 25.1, we hadn't seen any problems. However, in 25.2, even though this environment variable is added to the System Variable (can see by Start > Edit the system environment variables), it is not available to any other programs including Windows Power Shell and Command Prompt. But other environment variables like ANSYSEM_ROOT252 do not have is problem - right after the installation they are readily available for all the programs.

SIWAVE_INSTALL_DIR also suffers the same problem. Do you know if these environment variables are handled differently (like added at a later stage or something) than the regular environment variables like ANSYSEM_ROOT252? If so, could this be fixed?

If I restart the PC, then both SIMPLORER_HOME and SIWAVE_INSTALL_DIR are available for all programs.  But we don't think asking customers to restart every time after the installation is not a good idea since the installer doesn't require a restart.

We use this SIMPLORER_HOME for Simulink Coder (to build Twin Builder model DLL for users' Simulink design). We could use ANSYSEM_ROOT<Ver> instead, but the build script needs to be updated for every release. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

title: Camera GT metadata when serialization is disabled are duplicated
description:
DESCRIPTION:
Data :

Notes:
QA DATA : \\vlbfs1\Data Repository\Incident Reports\VSS\camera GT output data entries duplicated per time stamp in shm

Note CGR: Ensure "serialize_data": false in simulation parameters to disable serialization.

Steps to reproduce:
  1. Run vss with arguments - p 20000 -d 50000
  2. Run the scenario given to you in data
  3. Use a dataaccess client to get notification from databyidentifier (you can use for QA validation the sample in data )

    BUG  :

    we have two ids with same metadata




Expected behavior:
As quoted in the fix of bug Bug 1260145: camera GT output data entries duplicated per time stamp in shm
"with serialisation disabled we store raw image bytes and a separate serialised ground-truth (we must serialise GT because there is no raw representation)."

so the metadata should reflect what we get from the output it means :

  • one metadata for raw format 
  • one metadata for GT format
Reproducible (always, never, often, sometimes): 
always

Machine configuration:
Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version):
  • OS: N/A
  • GPU: N/A
  • Driver GPU: N/A
  • Hardware specific: N/A

==============================================

CLOSING SUMMARY:

Cause (if regression set an VRXP_REGRESSION tag):
When serialization is disabled, the metadata information was duplicated when creating the metadata for the color map (which is the only output which can be non-serialized), and the metadata for the other outputs (which are serialized).

Solution:
Fix how the metadata are produced, by totally separating the color map from the other outputs. 

Impacts (if there is a risk set an AVX_RISK_HIGH, AVX_RISK_MEDIUM or AVX_RISK_LOW tag):

QA Validation:

Doc:

GDR 22/05/2025 KIL documented in 2025 R2 in AVxcelerate Sensors Simulator Users Guide

Content: "Camera - When  Camera Ground Truth Parameters are set in the camera simulation parameters, and the serialize data parameter is set to false, the metadata sent in the notification to the data access client does not  precisely indicate the format of the data according to the dataId.  Metadata relevant to both Ground Truth Output Data and RAW image data is present for each notification. (TFS 1270686)"

Preview link - for internal use only: Known Issues > Sensor Outputs

Link to official helpsite that will be up-to-date on 2025 R2 FCA (leads to 404 page before FCA): Known Issues > Sensor Outputs

title: Debug CS FMU needs extra dependent release DLLs due to ComponentSystem DLL
description:
When compiling all inclusive CS FMU from a debug build the following DLLs are not copied to the FMU:
  • libssl-3-x64.dll
  • libcrypto-3-x64.dll
  • zlib1.dll.
The reason is these are only dependent for ComponentSystem.<ver>,dll coming from Ansys (not EBU). This ComponentSystem DLL is a release DLL  since EBU does not get a debug version of ComponentSystem.

Simplorer.json has the following configuration:
"libssl-3-x64.dll, libssl-3-x64-MDd.dll",
"libcrypto-3-x64.dll, libcrypto-3-x64-MDd.dll",
"zlib1.dll, zlibd1.dll",

Suggestion: To mitigate this issue, Simplorer.json can be provided with additional flag both such that both release and debug versions are copied for Debug build (only for debug not for release).

"libssl-3-x64.dll, libssl-3-x64-MDd.dll, both",
"libcrypto-3-x64.dll, libcrypto-3-x64-MDd.dll, both",
"zlib1.dll, zlibd1.dll, both",

Issue found while creating auto tests for customer Bug 1233639
Issue reproduced when scenario executed remotely with VPN and from office without VPN

Blocking creation of automatic test for customer Bug 1233639

FDS: Problem not limited to speos tester, can happen with any HPC simulation with sequence layering

Regression (if so, last known build/version where it was working):
Issue reproduced on 25R2 (2025.2.1.31394) and 26R1 (2026.1.0.31522-beta)

Steps to reproduce:
  1. run with speos tester tool the test attached (DATA.zip)
  2. select CPU HPC run ; the test neverends:

  3. issue not reproduced with speos tester CPU local, and from speos tester CPU or speos tester CPU HPC
Expected behavior:
Simulation should end and give similar result than CPU run without HPC

Reproducible (always, never, often, sometimes): 
always

Provide any relevant information about hardware or system software (RAM, nb CPU cores, hyper-threading, GPU model or sound adapter model and driver version):
Windows 11 24H2


CLOSING SUMMARY:

Cause (if regression set a SPEOS_REGRESSION tag):
Mishandling of sequence merge when a large number of sequence is handled but not all process have yet reached this maximum number (eg: max seq = 500 but different HPC process have only identified 200, 450 bc they have not yet converged)

Solution:
Broadcast final number of threads from rank 0 to force all rank to have same number of layer in case found sequence is lower than number of sequence given by user

Impacts (if there is a risk set a SPEOS_RISK_HIGH, SPEOS_RISK_MEDIUM, or SPEOS_RISK_LOW tag):
HPC CPU simulation with sensor separated by sequence with number of sequence lower than number of sequence given by user

Notes:
FDS 07302025: reproduced the infinite test but was not systematic, when a break point in CreateFile was set the test ran without any issue
Simulation stops around 90% and then gets stuck. Debug with child processes --> mpi thread seems to be lost --> mergesensors seems to be the point of problem --> 4 maps with diff layered map sizes
Able to bypass this issue by using 40 000 000 rays instead of 10 000 000 --> each HPC process should have the same number of rays as the equivalent CPU simulation
Problem not limited to speos tester, can happen with any HPC simulation with sequence layering

Validation:
Thanks to dev bypass (increasing rays nb to 4Mrays), I could capitalize the iniital test whose capitalization had conduced to this bug (speos tester 2106) even if the issue is not yet fixed PR 14294

title: DPF Sound: Octave/Third Octave levels computed by DPF Sound using time signal do not exactly match with SAS levels
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
pySoundDPF: Octave/Third Octave levels computed by DPF using time signal do not match with SAS (little differences, and some higher differences in the upper frequency bands)

Data:
Python files, WAV signal and exported levels from SAS.

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
SAS Usage:
Start a new session of SAS, open the attached WAV file "Acceleration_with_Tacho.wav".
Compute spectrum and convert to octave band. 
This octave levels can be exported to text file.
Exported text files for Octave and Third Octave are attached here.

DPF usage: "compute_one_third_octave_levels_from_signal"
Use the attached python script to use the same signal and compute octave levels using the signal.
Path to sound dpf dll and wav file will need to eb updated for local use.
It will print the Octave/Third Octave dB levels.
When compared with values from SAS we can see a mismatch in last band for Octave and last four bands for Third octave.--> BUG

Third Octave comparison:



Expected behavior:
As we are using the same time signal to compute Octave/Third Octave levels should be same from SAS and DPF Sound.

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
The differences were due to the fact that in SAS (and not in DPF Sound), a fade-in is applied before computing the 1/3-octave levels in order to avoid artificially inflated higher-frequency band levels when the input signal does not start at 0 (because, typically, they could be calculated on a chunk of signal, that could then start at any value; but technically any opened signal could also start at a nonzero value).

Solution:
This fade-in operation is now moved into the framework such that it is always applied regardless of the application. SAS-returned values are not affected, but DPF Sound-returned values are now adjusted to match SAS values.

Impacts:
Although it should probably go unnoticed in the large majority of cases ,in DPF Sound, the modified (1/3-)octave levels calculation may also affect returned values for:
  • Loudness ISO532-1 (stationary and time-varying)
  • Sharpness (stationary and time-varying)
  • Articulation index (AI)
  • Sound power level (SWL)
The extent of the deviation depends on the signal. 
As it only affects the first 10 ms, the effect is expected to be larger for shorter signals. 
It also appears to be larger as the overall level decreases: 
  • hardly noticeable (less than 0.1 dB) for "usual" acoustic levels (eg 50-80 dBSPL), 
  • a few dB for absolute levels in the range 0-20 dBSPL, 
  • up to 10 dB when the absolute level is around -20/-30 dBSPL.

import os

title: Effect of high velocity on Magnetic flux density in TEAM Problem 9 Simulation in Maxwell
description:
In the TEAM problem 9, the objective is determining the effect of high velocity on normal and tangential magnetic flux density (B) for both ferromagnetic and nonmagnetic material for two models. The model is set for different velocities: 0 m/s, 1 m/s, 10 m/s, and 100 m/s, as shown in the figure below (an example of the case for ferromagnetic material and measurement of Bz along L2), B does not follow the data points in the reference at higher velocities, specifically at 100 m/s. 

It seems Maxwell results do not  accurately show the effect of high velocity. Here is how I obtained the results from Maxwell: 
  • For example at V= 100 m/s, the time step is 1 ms. The velocity in MotionSetup is set to 100 m/s. Therefore, after 1 ms, the coil moves 100 mm. In the table of results for Br and Bz, I get (100 mm + x ) points where x is the required distance from the surface of the coil (0.1r, 0.5r, etc.) at the time B is at its maximum value (Bpeak/ sqrt(2)) which is 5ms in this simulation.
We also enabled the eddy current setting but it didn't affect the results. The aedt files as well as the ppt file explaining the results are attached for your reference. I appreciate your consideration on this issue. 

@Hui Niu 
@Mohammad Shahabbasi

title: Loft API creates surface body instead of solid body
description:
Lofting two closed circle profiles creates surface body when it should create a solid. Here's the python script to reproduce:
import System.Collections.Generic
from System.Collections.Generic import ICollection

c1 = Circle.Create(Frame.World, .005)
cs1 = CurveSegment.Create(c1, Interval.Create(0, 2*math.pi))

z_offset = .02
frame2 = Frame.Create(Point.Create(0, 0, z_offset), Direction.DirX, Direction.DirY)
c2 = Circle.Create(frame2, .01)
cs2 = CurveSegment.Create(c2, Interval.Create(0, 2*math.pi))

profiles = List[ICollection[ITrimmedCurve]]()
cs1_list = List[ITrimmedCurve]()
cs1_list.Add(cs1)
profiles.Add(cs1_list)

cs2_list = List[ITrimmedCurve]()
cs2_list.Add(cs2)
profiles.Add(cs2_list)

DesignBody.Create(GetRootPart(), "tube", Body.LoftProfiles(profiles, False, False))

Text description:
NON-CI Builds produced by pipelines for SAS and JLT do not update version number

After 17th July 2024: build numbers are the same for SAS, JLT and DPF

build numbers are always incremented, and can NEVER be the same for two folders (even for different applications)

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
DPF_Sound pipeline was still correctly updating build number, and was executed first (at 1 am)
SAS and JLT were not updating build number correctly, because of a wrong (?) syntax leading to only READ (and not UPDATE) the build number. However, as they were executed AFTER DPF_Sound, the build number may have been incremented from one day to another.

Solution:
Use exactly the same syntax in SAS and JLT scripts than in DPF_Sound script.

title: JLT - Build pipeline problem: impossible to run the pipeline if Agent Name is set and CI_BUILD is selected - might be more general (all yaml build pipelines)
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
In JLT build pipeline, if CI_BUILD is selected in ADO's GUI, and if AgentName is set different from Any, we get an error when clicking on Run.
If CI_BUILD is selected and AgentName is Any: everything is OK.

Not tried:
  • CI_BUILD not selected, AgentName set
  • SAS or DPF_Sound pipelines
EDIT AMD 2025/04/09: Issue is reproduced in SAS and DPFS, and regardless of CI_BUILD state

Data:

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
Create new run of the JLT, SAS or DPFS pipeline
Check the setting CI_BUILD
Check AgentName setting to AEPBUILD001 (or AEPBUILD002).

you get this error:
-> pipeline cannot be run

Expected behavior:
No error, pipelines run with the specified settings.

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
Wrong demands syntax in yaml scripts: two demands section must not be encountered twice in the same stage in pipeline run. But when you select a specific agent, you would encounter a first section with the common requirement (eg VIsualStudioBuilds) and then, passing an if condition on the agent, you would encounter a second testing agent name, which caused the error


Solution:
Restored old syntax where the two demands sections are defined under two mutually exclusive if conditions, such that you can never encounter both section within the same pipeline run
