Hi All,

I am currently working on a workflow (see image below) to extract von Mises field values from an Abaqus .odb file using the ETK node in oSL 25R1 (as part of oSL AFT).



Specifically, I aim to retrieve von Mises stress values for S4R elements at a specific location, namely the SNEG (shell bottom surface). While I am able to check and visualize the extracted values in oSL (as in the two images below),

The following error is returned:

CODBFieldOutputVariable::Initialize : Exception : No data available for this selection (from RPC dispatch side).
```

Notably, this issue does not occur when working with nodal fields — it seems to be specific to stress invariants derived from the S tensor.

I confirm I am able to extract von Mises stress values by means of the attached python code (extractVonMises_Test.py) and by automatically generating a report by means of "Generate Report" batch node in the attached workflow (see CrashTest_Cyl_Box.rpt file attached for an example of generated report).

Can you help me identify where the problem originates from?

Thank you!
Margherita

A lot of modification must be done directly in the source code (framework), in the projects (from subsystem:windows to subsystem:console to avoid a link problem). Currently we have a problem with the conversion from QString to StdString (provoke a crash). A way to avoid the problem:

	auto l_Debug_pathGenericDataLocation = QStandardPaths::standardLocations(QStandardPaths::GenericDataLocation);
	l_Debug_pathGenericDataLocation[0].append("/").append(OLD_ORGANISATIONNAME);

	auto debug1 = l_Debug_pathGenericDataLocation[0];
	char* toto = new char[debug1.length() + 1];
	toto[debug1.length()] = '\0'; // Null-terminate the string
	for (unsigned int l_i = 0; l_i < debug1.length(); l_i++)
	{
		toto[l_i] = debug1[l_i].toLatin1();
	}
	Optis::String l_pathString(toto);

	delete[] toto;

	return l_pathString;

but it's probably a bad workaround. Crashes are probably caused by a bad configuration of the project.

title: AFT: Mechanical Meshing: Google Taiwan > Multizone Thin sweep failing on simple model
GenerateModelDef generates u1_model.mesher_result file with slightly wrong Metrics for some LC
description:
This is the followup bug after the fix of Bug 1209403: GenerateModelDef generates wrong mesher_result file with zero Metrics

My test shows that the metrics in the new U1_model.mesher_result file is slightly bigger than the original metrics for some layout components. This is affecting HFSS simulation since we rely on this information to create mesh fusion envelopes, and the inaccurate size may cause error during mesh fusion.

Here is an example. The attached LC1_1_edbWorkflow.aedtz is the project that we originally used to extract information by calling GMD. This project is created by directly importing the edb file. The output file is model.mesher_result

In comparison, LC1_1_aedbcompWorkflow.aedtz is the project that we created using the new workflow where we convert the edb file into .aedmcomp file and then import it in to an empty layout design. We call GMD on this project and the U1_model.mesher_result is the output.

title: Display Cell Residuals using cell registers
description:
Method 1 – Cell Register via Threshold Percent (GUI-based):

Via Solution → Cell Registers, it is possible to create a residual register for specific equations (e.g., continuity, x/y/z velocity, kkk, ω\omegaω).

By specifying a Threshold Percent (e.g., 90), Fluent includes the top 10 % of cells with the highest local residuals in the register.


Method 2 – Residual Field Activation via TUI (/solve/set/expert):

Using the TUI command: /solve/set/expert


and enabling the option “Keep temporary solver memory from being freed”, Fluent makes cell-wise residual values available as a field variable for post-processing.

title: [regression] SAS - Sound Composer: for a source of type Spectrum, the display of the spectrum imported from a PSD in a txt file with AnsysSound_Spectrum header is incorrect
description:
DESCRIPTION ----
Text description:
The spectrum imported as a Source of type Spectrum in the Sound Composer is not displayed correctly, which can make the user think the data used for the sound generation of this track is not the correct one (and actually the sound generation looks correct).
Note: works well in 2024 R2. Broken since 2025 R1.

Data:
Example 00_AnsysHeader_PSD_dB.txt (PSD in dB/Hz)
Example 00_AnsysHeader_PSD_Pa2-Hz.txt (PSD in Pa2/Hz)

Reproducible: always

Steps to reproduce:
Open the Sound Composer.
Create new track. Select new source, with type Spectrum.
Load the attached file Example 00_AnsysHeader_PSD_dB.txt.
In the Source tab, click the Display button: 


The displayed spectrum is not the one expected: the levels are incorrect, and the maximum frequency is 214 Hz instead of 3002.5 Hz.

When the same file is imported from the menu File > Import > Import spectrum from text file..., the displayed spectrum is correct:



Same problem with the second file attached: Example 00_AnsysHeader_PSD_Pa2-Hz.txt

Notes:
  • The same problem probably happens for every unit corresponding to a PSD in the txt file.
  • I have not checked if the same issue happens with an Autospectrum -> NO
  • Looks like the signal generated by the Sound composer has the correct spectrum!

Expected behavior:
The spectrum displayed is the same as the one in the source file.
The display is done with the same unit (and hence the same type) as the one in the source file.

CLOSING SUMMARY ----
Cause (if regression include [regression] in the title):
Data causing this bug are not regularly spaced.
For display, they are considered as if they were regularly spaced, starting at 0Hz -> wrong display

Solution:
As PSD data may not be regularly spaced, we choose to display the same data as the one used for sound generation: the regularly spaced interpolated PSD.

Also, there is no issue when via removal is disabled (see KeepVias_Padstack design). It is not necessary to look at the StackedVias_Padstack design for this defect, but it does demonstrate the same plane removal behavior with some different via configurations.

I also ran the same designs with classic vias drawn in a via layer and the behavior was identical. Via Groups look a bit different, but I suspect they are not drawn correctly (no pads). I'll check with @Aman Samaiyar on those next week and follow up once we have a good Via Group design.
